raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

This is our **draft reference implementation of [RFC #57103: Programmable KV Cache](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57103)**, shared for design discussion and implementation review. It does not close the RFC or claim complete acceptance.

Agentic sessions span multiple inference requests, tool pauses, and branches. The RFC lets an application express lifecycle and cache intent through the existing `KvHintsEnvelope`, while the engine resolves targets, approves resources, executes operations, and reports actual completion.

### How this implementation maps to the RFC

- **Common control and logical state:** request-attached hints and independent Python/HTTP control share the envelope, dispatcher, and engine approval path. Hash/session/continuation/range selectors resolve logical content separately from physical residency. Results are correlated by message/action IDs, with bounded replay, queries, ACK, cancellation, and engine epochs. Existing backend-owned KVCR payloads retain opaque forwarding.
- **Execution through existing cache infrastructure:** `SET_PRIORITY`, `COPY_TO`, and `MOVE_TO` use `KVCacheManager`/`BlockPool` and CPU/Mooncake Store adapters. GPU-source operations run at successful request completion before references are released; accepted transfers can outlive the request. COPY publishes reusable GPU content only after all participating ranks finish. MOVE stores first and reclaims eligible source copies afterward. Shared loads share reservations and transfer holds; a resume can wait for an existing load.
- **Optional policies and rollout integration:** retention, tool-wait movement, and quota/prefix-reuse scheduling consume engine observations and submit proposals through the same approval boundary. Explicit commands keep their meaning. Startup configuration controls policy registration. The benchmark harness connects real verl `ToolAgentLoop` calls, tools, token logprobs, response masks, and rewards; weight-update checks exercise draining, invalidation, and cache namespace isolation.

Implementation contracts: [native primitives and lifecycle](https://github.com/zhhangBian/vllm-note/blob/rfc-hint/vllm/v1/kv_hints/README.md). Reproduction: [benchmark commands](https://github.com/zhhangBian/vllm-note/blob/rfc-hint/benchmarks/programmable_kv_cache/README.md).

### Current conclusions

Recorded local experiments use Qwen3.8-27B BF16, two A100 80GB GPUs, TP=2, concurrency 16, and 32 rollouts from 8 GSM8K questions. Each fixed-work replay has 113 model calls and 8,121 output tokens. The principal comparisons use three runs per configuration and report median throughput relative to native APC at the **same GPU KV budget**; movement additionally uses a host Store.

| GPU KV per GPU          | Configuration                 | Native / reference elapsed | Throughput change |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------: | ----------------: |
| 2 GiB, constrained      | Quota/prefix-reuse scheduling |          449.06 / 219.63 s |           +104.5% |
| 2 GiB, constrained      | Retention + movement + quota  |          449.06 / 247.60 s |            +81.4% |
| 8 GiB, working set fits | Retention + movement + quota  |            54.09 / 56.13 s |             -3.6% |

These measurements support executable lifecycle/resource contracts and a scheduling benefit under constrained KV capacity. They do **not** establish an additional benefit from movement/composition over quota alone, or a general serving speedup. The 2 GiB setting is an artificial pressure diagnostic. When the working set fits, both arms have zero preemptions and equal cache hits; control overhead produces a regression.

Separate live tool runs took 452.37 / 288.73 / 214.34 s for native/full-policy/quota, each scoring 32/32 rewards. These are single runs with different generated trajectories and only 8 independent questions. Fixed replay reruns model generation but does not rerun tools or evaluate rewards.

The [experiment report](https://github.com/zhhangBian/vllm-note/blob/rfc-hint/docs/programmable-kvc/rollout-report-2026-10-12.md) records variability, tail-latency regressions, missing Store objects, methodology, and unfinished acceptance. Raw traces/logs remain local and are not included in this PR.

### Related work and remaining scope

Duplicate checks covered #57103's discussion, open PRs referencing it, and KV-hint/programmable-cache searches. [#58198](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58198) supplies a minimal request-free CPU-to-GPU primitive; [#59714](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59714) and [#38514](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38514) cover retention priority. This reference has a broader purpose: a runnable control/lifecycle/resource/execution path plus policy and rollout experiments. Its overlapping primitive, dispatcher, and priority code needs consolidation with those contributions before upstream merge. The experimental COPY/MOVE schema follows the direction discussed in #59708 and remains open to revision.

This draft preserves development baseline `30f5c01d4ebb5c493ed86195db24d0ec5b3ce3d7` and currently has conflicts with upstream `main`. Rebase and validation against current `main` remain open. Other gaps include the full prediction/fairness/outage/restart matrix, a fresh final 128-question evaluation, other models/layouts, Dynamo/llm-d integration, and full RL trainer/optimizer performance. CPU control requires one block per chunk; native Mooncake movement requires PCP=DCP=1. Cold-tier retention/deletion and mixed native/backend envelopes are unsupported.

## Validation

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,3 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/test_kv_hint_control.py \
  tests/v1/test_kv_hint_state.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_kv_control.py \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/kv_control/test_api.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --from-ref 30f5c01d4ebb5c493ed86195db24d0ec5b3ce3d7 --to-ref rfc-hint --show-diff-on-failure
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --from-ref 30f5c01d4ebb5c493ed86195db24d0ec5b3ce3d7 --to-ref rfc-hint
openspec validate programmable-kv-cache --strict
```

The recorded regression result is **680 passed**, with 14 PyTorch deprecation warnings. The implementation files tested are identical to those in this branch; the subsequent history edit changes attribution trailers only. The full branch pre-commit checks passed. Python 3.12 type checks and OpenSpec strict validation passed on the same implementation. The model and rollout measurements above are earlier experimental results, not newly rerun evaluations.

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, documentation, and PR preparation. The human submitter has confirmed reviewing every changed line and personally running the relevant tests.

+# Programmable KV cache benchmarks
+
+This experimental implementation follows [RFC #57103](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57103).
+The [interface reference](../../vllm/v1/kv_hints/README.md) describes native actions, lifecycle semantics, resource limits and supported layouts.
+Run the commands below from the repository root using the project virtual environment.
+Replace model, dataset and GPU arguments with resources available on your machine.
+Outputs under `benchmarks/programmable_kv_cache/results/` are ignored by Git.
+
+## Serving and functional validation
+
+Start a local server with prefix caching and native control enabled:
+
+```bash
+.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
+  --model /path/to/model \
+  --served-model-name kv-validation \
+  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
+  --max-model-len 4096 \
+  --enable-prefix-caching \
+  --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
+  --kv-control-config '{"engine_id":"kv-validation"}' \
+  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18083
+```
+
+To test CPU transfers, add this connector configuration:
+
+```bash
+--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":8589934592,"blocks_per_chunk":1}}'
+```
+
+For Mooncake transfers, install the matching wheel from `requirements/kv_connectors.txt`, start a Store master and save its client configuration:
+
+```bash
+.venv/bin/mooncake_master \
+  --rpc_address=127.0.0.1 --rpc_port=19151 \
+  --metrics_host=127.0.0.1 --metrics_port=19153 \
+  --enable_metric_reporting=false
+```
+
+```json
+{
+  "metadata_server": "P2PHANDSHAKE",
+  "master_server_address": "127.0.0.1:19151",
+  "protocol": "tcp",
+  "device_name": "",
+  "global_segment_size": "8GB",
+  "local_buffer_size": "256MB"
+}
+```
+
+Set `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH` to that file before starting the server, and add:
+
+```bash
+--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeStoreConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"enable_lookup":false,"enable_save":false,"save_decode_cache":false}}'
+```
+
+Disabling automatic connector lookup and save isolates the effects of explicit COPY/MOVE operations.
+Native Mooncake transfers require PCP=DCP=1 and targets aligned to every cache group's supported boundaries.
+CPU transfers require one block per chunk. Query `/v1/kv/capabilities` for the active layout and transfer directions.
+
+Exercise attached and independent operations, actual cache reuse and priority:
+
+```bash
+.venv/bin/python -m benchmarks.programmable_kv_cache.http_control \
+  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18083 \
+  --engine-id kv-validation \
+  --dataset /path/to/gsm8k \
+  --output /tmp/kv-control.json
+```
+
+The dataset is a downloaded GSM8K repository containing `main/*.parquet`.
+Use `--tier cpu` for the CPU connector, `--evaluation-samples 128` for the quality comparison, or `--destination-url` for a compatible second engine sharing the Store.
+For `http_control --policy`, replace the server's control configuration with:
+
+```bash
+--kv-control-config '{"engine_id":"kv-validation","policies":[{"name":"retention","implementation":"retention"},{"name":"movement","implementation":"tool_wait","options":{"tier":"mooncake"}}]}'
+```
+
+A completed signal receipt still requires collecting its separately identified derived operations.
+
+## Repeated rollout comparisons
+
+`verl_rollout.py` uses verl's `ToolAgentLoop`, executes tools and records generated tokens, logprobs, response masks, rewards and control outcomes.
+It requires an importable verl checkout and its Agent Loop dependencies.
+
+`run_rollout_matrix.py` starts and cleans up servers, a Mooncake Store and GPU sampling processes.
+It checks port ownership, warms the server, resets caches between runs, and records commands, source hashes, workload fingerprints and timing data.
+Without `--trace`, it collects a live trace before the timed fixed-work replays:
+
+```bash
+.venv/bin/python -m benchmarks.programmable_kv_cache.run_rollout_matrix \
+  --model /path/to/model --dataset /path/to/gsm8k \
+  --gpus 0,1 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 \
+  --prompts 64 --samples 4 --families 32 --fewshot 48 \
+  --concurrency 64 --max-num-seqs 64 \
+  --arms native,idle,noop,policy --repeats 3 \
+  --output-dir /tmp/kv-comparison
+```
+
+| Mode or option | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `native` | Native automatic prefix caching |
+| `idle` / `noop` | Controller enabled; controller plus connector enabled; neither sends hints |
+| `priority` / `movement` / `composed` | Application-issued priority, transfer, or combined commands |
+| `policy` | Signal-driven retention, movement and quota policies |
+| `--policy-components quota` | Isolate scheduling without a movement connector |
+| `--policy-components retention` | Isolate retention; can be combined with quota |
+| `--trace FILE` | Replay recorded inputs, output lengths and pauses |
+| `--live-after-replay` / `--live-only` | Run actual tool loops separately from replay measurements |
+| `--prediction-mode adaptive` | Estimate pauses from completed tool batches |
+| `--prediction-mode fixed --prediction-seconds N` | Use a fixed pause estimate |
+| `--oracle` | Use recorded future pauses during replay; label this diagnostic separately |
+| `--prefetch-on-admission` | Prepare queued sessions when selected by the scheduler |
+| `--movement-pressure-only` | Disable the movement pause-cost filter for an ablation |
+| `--cache-gib N` | Set an explicit GPU KV budget for a capacity diagnostic |
+| `--profile` | Collect CPU/GPU profiles separately from throughput runs; requires `yappi` |
+
+Use `--help` for policy thresholds, waiting budgets, generation settings and profiling windows.
+Compare configurations at the same GPU KV budget and report the additional host memory and CPU used by movement.
+Use separate output directories when changing policy components or workload settings.
+
+Fixed-work replay regenerates output using recorded input tokens and output lengths; it does not execute tools or compute rewards.
+Live trajectories can differ between configurations and require separate quality comparisons.
+Elapsed time includes client queueing, tool waits, control collection and transfer draining, and excludes startup and explicit warmup.
+GPU occupancy audits must cover the measured window. Profiled runs are excluded from ordinary throughput comparisons.
+
+```bash
+.venv/bin/python -m benchmarks.programmable_kv_cache.analyze_rollout \
+  --run native=/path/to/native.json.gz \
+  --run policy=/path/to/policy.json.gz \
+  --baseline native --output /tmp/kv-comparison.json
+```
+
+Repeat `--run` for repeated measurements under the same label.
+The analyzer checks equal workload fingerprints and serving conditions, and reports throughput, tail latency and forecast errors.
+For live quality, it separates reported rewards from complete final answers: a correct incidental number in truncated output does not establish a completed correct answer.
+
+## Additional validation tools
+
+| Module | Scope and required arguments |
+| --- | --- |
+| `evaluate` | Recomputed/APC model quality: `--model --dataset --output`; optionally `--enable-kv-control` |
+| `lifecycle` | Shared branches, TTL, cancellation and resume races: `--base-url --trace --output` |
+| `weight_update` | Real parameter update, invalidation and rollback: `--base-url --model --trace --output` |
+| `control_overhead` | CPU-only result polling and cached guidance: `--output` |
+| `run_recovery` | Managed server/Store validation: `--model --dataset --trace --output-dir`; optional `--lifecycle`, `--weight-update`, `--evaluation-samples 128` or `--cpu-evaluation-samples 128` |
+
+Invoke these as `.venv/bin/python -m benchmarks.programmable_kv_cache.MODULE`.
+`run_recovery --capacity-deferral-only` tests partial loads, budget refusal, retries and recomputation with a one-block load budget; it is a correctness diagnostic.
+Weight-update validation requires the same-host model checkpoint, an idle server, `--weight-transfer-config '{"backend":"ipc"}'`, `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1` and `VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1` on a locally bound server.
+It changes real GPU parameters and restores them; it does not run an optimizer.
+
+## Regression checks
+
+```bash
+.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
+  tests/v1/test_kv_hint_control.py \
+  tests/v1/test_kv_hint_state.py \
+  tests/v1/engine/test_kv_control.py \
+  tests/entrypoints/serve/kv_control/test_api.py \
+  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
+  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
+  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py -q
+```
+
+`tests/v1/kv_connector/mooncake_integration/test_store_buffers.py` additionally validates real Store transfers across two CUDA GPUs, including missing-rank and reset behavior.
+It requires the matching native Mooncake wheel and either a local master executable or `VLLM_TEST_MOONCAKE_MASTER`.
+Model evaluations and hardware-dependent transfer checks should accompany changes to cache contents or execution behavior.

+"""Compare complete equal-work runs and audit application control timing."""
+
+import argparse
+import gzip
+import hashlib
+import json
+import statistics
+from collections import defaultdict
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from benchmarks.programmable_kv_cache.client import answer_number
+
+
+def distribution(values):
+    values = sorted(values)
+    if not values:
+        return {"count": 0}
+    return {
+        "count": len(values),
+        "min": values[0],
+        "median": statistics.median(values),
+        "p95": values[min(len(values) - 1, int(len(values) * 0.95))],
+        "max": values[-1],
+    }
+
+
+def audit(path):
+    with gzip.open(path, "rt") as file:
+        report = json.load(file)
+    trajectories = defaultdict(list)
+    for row in report["requests"]:
+        trajectories[row["request_id"]].append(row)
+    pauses = []
+    for rows in trajectories.values():
+        rows.sort(key=lambda row: row["turn"])
+        pauses.extend(b["started"] - a["finished"] for a, b in zip(rows, rows[1:]))
+    episodes = report.get("episodes", [])
+    quality = None
+    if episodes and all("reward" in row for row in episodes):
+        endings = [
+            (episode, trajectories.get(episode["request_id"], [{}])[-1])
+            for episode in episodes
+        ]
+        complete = {
+            episode["request_id"]
+            for episode, final in endings
+            if "####" in final.get("text", "") and final.get("finish_reason") == "stop"
+        }
+        quality = {
+            "episodes": len(episodes),
+            "reported_correct": sum(row["reward"] for row in episodes),
+            "completed_final_correct": sum(
+                episode["request_id"] in complete
+                and episode.get("expected") is not None
+                and answer_number(final["text"]) == episode["expected"]
+                for episode, final in endings
+            ),
+            "missing_final_marker": sum(
+                "####" not in final.get("text", "") for _, final in endings
+            ),
+            "final_length_limited": sum(
+                final.get("finish_reason") == "length" for _, final in endings
+            ),
+            "reported_correct_without_completed_final": sum(
+                episode["reward"]
+                for episode, _ in endings
+                if episode["request_id"] not in complete
+            ),
+            "incomplete_final_request_ids": [
+                episode["request_id"]
+                for episode, _ in endings
+                if episode["request_id"] not in complete
+            ],
+        }
+    signals = defaultdict(list)
+    for row in report["controls"]:
+        if "driver_signal" in row:
+            signals[row["driver_signal"]].append(row.get("driver_seconds", 0))
+    summary = report.get("summary", {})
+    forecasts = report.get("tool_waits", [])
+    errors = [r["predicted_seconds"] - r["actual_seconds"] for r in forecasts]
+    manifest_path = path.parent / "matrix.json"
+    manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text()) if manifest_path.exists() else {}
+    config = dict(manifest.get("config", {}))
+    for command in manifest.get("commands", []):
+        if "vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server" not in command:
+            continue
+        for key, flag in (
+            ("max_num_seqs", "--max-num-seqs"),
+            ("batch_tokens", "--max-num-batched-tokens"),
+        ):
+            if flag in command:
+                config[key] = int(command[command.index(flag) + 1])
+        break
+    return {
+        "path": str(path.resolve()),
+        "sha256": hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
+        "source_revision": report.get("source_revision"),
+        "source_hashes": report.get("source_hashes"),
+        "passed": report["passed"],
+        "seconds": report.get("seconds"),
+        "workload_sha256": summary.get("workload_sha256"),
+        "pause_seconds": distribution(pauses),
+        "pauses_below_100ms": sum(value < 0.1 for value in pauses),
+        "signal_seconds": {
+            name: distribution(values) for name, values in signals.items()
+        },
+        "forecast_error_seconds": distribution(errors),
+        "forecast_absolute_error_seconds": distribution([abs(v) for v in errors]),
+        "forecast_underestimates": sum(v < 0 for v in errors),
+        "forecast_overestimates": sum(v > 0 for v in errors),
+        "client_queue_seconds": distribution(
+            [r["client_queue_seconds"] for r in report.get("episodes", [])]
+        ),
+        "summary": summary,
+        "quality": quality,
+        "instrumented": config.get("profile", False),
+        "conditions": {
+            key: config.get(key)
+            for key in (
+                "model",
+                "gpus",
+                "gpu_memory_utilization",
+                "cache_gib",
+                "concurrency",
+                "max_num_seqs",
+                "batch_tokens",
+                "max_context",
+                "enforce_eager",
+                "disable_custom_all_reduce",
+                "replay_pause_floor",
+            )
+        }
+        if config
+        else None,
+    }
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--run", action="append", required=True, help="LABEL=report.json.gz"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--baseline", default="native")
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    runs = defaultdict(list)
+    for entry in args.run:
+        label, path = entry.split("=", 1)
+        runs[label].append(audit(Path(path)))
+    fingerprints = {row["workload_sha256"] for group in runs.values() for row in group}
+    comparable = len(fingerprints) == 1 and None not in fingerprints
+    complete = all(row["passed"] for group in runs.values() for row in group)
+    conditions = {
+        json.dumps(r["conditions"], sort_keys=True)
+        for group in runs.values()
+        for r in group
+        if not r["instrumented"]
+    }
+    equal_conditions = len(conditions) == 1 and "null" not in conditions
+    comparison = {}
+    if comparable and complete and equal_conditions and args.baseline in runs:
+        if any(r["instrumented"] for r in runs[args.baseline]):
+            raise ValueError("Timing baseline must not be instrumented")
+        baseline = statistics.median(r["seconds"] for r in runs[args.baseline])
+        baseline_families = defaultdict(list)
+        for row in runs[args.baseline]:
+            for family, values in row["summary"].get("family_latency", {}).items():
+                baseline_families[family].append(values["p95_seconds"])
+        for label, group in runs.items():
+            if any(r["instrumented"] for r in group):
+                continue
+            seconds = [r["seconds"] for r in group]
+            families = defaultdict(list)
+            for row in group:
+                for family, values in row["summary"].get("family_latency", {}).items():
+                    families[family].append(values["p95_seconds"])
+            ratios = {
+                family: statistics.median(values)
+                / statistics.median(baseline_families[family])
+                for family, values in families.items()
+                if family in baseline_families
+                and statistics.median(baseline_families[family]) > 0
+            }
+            comparison[label] = {
+                "seconds": distribution(seconds),
+                "throughput_gain_percent": 100
+                * (baseline / statistics.median(seconds) - 1),
+                "ttft_p99_seconds": distribution(
+                    r["summary"]["ttft_p99"] for r in group
+                ),
+                "worst_family_p95_seconds": distribution(
+                    max(
+                        f["p95_seconds"]
+                        for f in r["summary"]["family_latency"].values()
+                    )
+                    for r in group
+                    if r["summary"].get("family_latency")
+                ),
+                "family_p95_ratio_to_baseline": ratios,
+                "families_with_higher_p95": sum(v > 1 for v in ratios.values()),
+            }
+    result = {
+        "equal_work": comparable,
+        "all_complete": complete,
+        "equal_timing_conditions": equal_conditions,
+        "comparison": comparison,
+        "runs": dict(runs),
+        "limitations": (
+            "Equal token inputs/output lengths do not establish equal sampling, "
+            "hardware occupancy, profiling or configuration. Inspect run manifests. "
+            "Pause intervals include client work; signal intervals include RPC, "
+            "polling and ACK time, and are not device transfer durations."
+        ),
+    }
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
+    print(
+        json.dumps(
+            {key: result[key] for key in ("equal_work", "all_complete", "comparison")},
+            indent=2,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Small control helpers shared by the real-server examples."""
+
+import time
+from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation
+from typing import Any
+
+import regex as re
+
+ACTIVE = {"received", "queued", "accepted", "running"}
+
+
+def answer_number(text: str) -> str | None:
+    values = re.findall(r"-?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?", text.split("####")[-1])
+    if not values:
+        return None
+    try:
+        return str(Decimal(values[-1].replace(",", "")).normalize())
+    except InvalidOperation:
+        return None
+
+
+def envelope(message_id: str, kind: str, payload: dict[str, Any], version: str = "1.0"):
+    return {
+        "protocol_version": "0.1",
+        "message_id": message_id,
+        "actions": [
+            {
+                "action_id": "action",
+                "action_type": kind,
+                "action_version": version,
+                "payload": payload,
+            }
+        ],
+    }
+
+
+def wait_operation(
+    call,
+    message_id: str,
+    action_id: str = "action",
+    *,
+    timeout: float = 120,
+    acknowledge: bool = False,
+):
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+        result = call("operation", {"message_id": message_id, "action_id": action_id})
+        if result["message_id"] != message_id or result["action_id"] != action_id:
+            raise AssertionError("Control result lost caller correlation")
+        if result["status"] not in ACTIVE:
+            if acknowledge:
+                call("acknowledge", {"message_id": message_id})
+            return result
+        time.sleep(0.02)
+    raise TimeoutError(f"KV operation {message_id}/{action_id} did not finish")

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Measure CPU result polling and cached policy guidance; no GPU serving work."""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import statistics
+import time
+from functools import partial
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config.kv_control import KVControlConfig, KVPolicyConfig
+from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_manager import KVCacheManager
+from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import BlockHash, make_block_hash_with_group_id
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import (
+    FullAttentionSpec,
+    KVCacheConfig,
+    KVCacheGroupSpec,
+)
+from vllm.v1.kv_hints.control import ControlContext, OperationRegistry, OperationStatus
+from vllm.v1.kv_hints.controller import NativeKVController
+from vllm.v1.kv_hints.policy_runtime import KVPolicyRuntime
+from vllm.v1.kv_hints.protocol import KvHintAction, KvHintsEnvelope
+from vllm.v1.kv_hints.retention import RetentionDeclarations
+from vllm.v1.kv_hints.state import SessionPrefixIndex
+
+
+def measure(function, iterations, repeats):
+    samples = []
+    for _ in range(repeats):
+        start = time.perf_counter_ns()
+        for _ in range(iterations):
+            function()
+        samples.append((time.perf_counter_ns() - start) / iterations / 1000)
+    return {"median_us": statistics.median(samples), "samples_us": samples}
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True, type=Path)
+    parser.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=5)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if args.repeats < 1:
+        parser.error("--repeats must be positive")
+    report = {
+        "scope": "cpu_only_no_requests",
+        "repeats": args.repeats,
+        "measurements": {},
+    }
+    results = report["measurements"]
+    context = ControlContext("engine", "epoch", "native")
+    for records in (64, 4096):
+        registry = OperationRegistry("engine", engine_epoch="epoch", clock=lambda: 0.0)
+        for i in range(records):
+            result = registry.submit(
+                KvHintsEnvelope(
+                    "0.1",
+                    str(i),
+                    [
+                        KvHintAction("a", "signal", "1", {}),
+                    ],
+                ),
+                context,
+            ).results[0]
+            registry.update(result, OperationStatus.COMPLETED)
+        results[f"poll_{records}_results"] = measure(
+            partial(registry.get, "0", "a"),
+            3000,
+            args.repeats,
+        )
+    index = SessionPrefixIndex("namespace", "epoch")
+    controller = NativeKVController(registry, index, RetentionDeclarations(index))
+    settings = KVControlConfig(
+        policies=[KVPolicyConfig(name="quota", implementation="quota")]
+    )
+    for blocks in (10000, 100000):
+        spec = FullAttentionSpec(
+            block_size=16, num_kv_heads=1, head_size=16, dtype=torch.float16
+        )
+        manager = KVCacheManager(
+            KVCacheConfig(blocks, [], [KVCacheGroupSpec(["layer"], spec)]),
+            max_model_len=128,
+            scheduler_block_size=16,
+            hash_block_size=16,
+        )
+        runtime = KVPolicyRuntime(
+            settings,
+            controller,
+            manager,
+            lambda: (),
+            clock=lambda: 0.0,
+            wall_clock=lambda: 0.0,
+        )
+        runtime.observe_requests()
+        results[f"cached_guidance_{blocks}_blocks"] = measure(
+            runtime.observe_requests, 100, args.repeats
+        )
+        results[f"fresh_observation_{blocks}_blocks"] = measure(
+            runtime.observation, 100, args.repeats
+        )
+        pool = manager.block_pool
+        allocated = pool.get_new_blocks(blocks - 1)
+        for block in allocated:
+            key = make_block_hash_with_group_id(
+                BlockHash(block.block_id.to_bytes(8, "big")), 0
+            )
+            pool.cache_transferred_block(block, key, 16)
+        pool.free_blocks(allocated)
+        results[f"populated_observation_{blocks}_blocks"] = measure(
+            runtime.observation, 100, args.repeats
+        )
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
+    print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""Compare model accuracy with real prefix reuse and forced recomputation."""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import random
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+import pyarrow.parquet as pq
+
+from benchmarks.programmable_kv_cache.client import answer_number
+from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--model", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--dataset",
+        type=Path,
+        required=True,
+        help="Downloaded GSM8K repository containing main/*.parquet",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--num-samples", type=int, default=128)
+    parser.add_argument("--num-fewshot", type=int, default=8)
+    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
+    parser.add_argument("--tensor-parallel-size", type=int, default=2)
+    parser.add_argument("--max-model-len", type=int, default=4096)
+    parser.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=1024)
+    memory = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
+    memory.add_argument("--kv-cache-memory-bytes", type=int)
+    memory.add_argument("--gpu-memory-utilization", type=float, default=0.5)
+    parser.add_argument("--min-accuracy", type=float, default=0.8)
+    parser.add_argument("--max-accuracy-drop", type=float, default=0.01)
+    parser.add_argument("--enable-kv-control", action="store_true")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if not 0 < args.gpu_memory_utilization <= 1:
+        parser.error("gpu-memory-utilization must be in (0, 1]")
+    train = pq.read_table(
+        args.dataset / "main/train-00000-of-00001.parquet"
+    ).to_pylist()
+    test = pq.read_table(args.dataset / "main/test-00000-of-00001.parquet").to_pylist()
+    if not 0 < args.num_samples <= len(test) or not 0 <= args.num_fewshot <= len(train):
+        parser.error("Invalid sample or few-shot count")
+    indices = random.Random(args.seed).sample(range(len(test)), args.num_samples)
+    examples = train[: args.num_fewshot]
+    llm_args = {
+        "model": args.model,
+        "tensor_parallel_size": args.tensor_parallel_size,
+        "max_model_len": args.max_model_len,
+        "max_num_seqs": 8,
+        "max_num_batched_tokens": 2048,
+        "kv_cache_memory_bytes": args.kv_cache_memory_bytes,
+        "gpu_memory_utilization": args.gpu_memory_utilization,
+        "enable_prefix_caching": True,
+        "mamba_cache_mode": "align",
+        "enforce_eager": True,
+        "disable_custom_all_reduce": True,
+        "dtype": "bfloat16",
+    }
+    if args.enable_kv_control:
+        llm_args["kv_control_config"] = {"engine_id": "evaluation"}
+    llm = LLM(**llm_args)
+    report: dict[str, Any] = {
+        "configuration": llm_args,
+        "seed": args.seed,
+        "num_fewshot": args.num_fewshot,
+        "prompt_format": "gsm8k_completion_cot",
+        "sampling": {"temperature": 0, "max_tokens": args.max_tokens},
+        "thresholds": {
+            "min_accuracy": args.min_accuracy,
+            "max_accuracy_drop": args.max_accuracy_drop,
+            "max_truncated_fraction": 0.01,
+        },
+        "indices": indices,
+        "runs": {},
+    }
+    try:
+        report["cache_groups"] = llm.llm_engine.engine_core.call_utility(
+            "get_kv_cache_group_metadata"
+        )
+        tokenizer = llm.get_tokenizer()
+        shared = "".join(
+            f"Question: {example['question']}\nAnswer: {example['answer']}\n\n"
+            for example in examples
+        )
+        shared_tokens = len(tokenizer.encode(shared, add_special_tokens=False))
+        assert shared_tokens >= max(g["block_size"] for g in report["cache_groups"]), (
+            "Few-shot prefix is too short to exercise this model's reusable boundaries"
+        )
+        prompts = [
+            {
+                "prompt_token_ids": tokenizer.encode(
+                    shared + f"Question: {test[i]['question']}\nAnswer:",
+                    add_special_tokens=False,
+                )
+            }
+            for i in indices
+        ]
+        assert (
+            max(len(p["prompt_token_ids"]) for p in prompts) + args.max_tokens
+            <= args.max_model_len
+        )
+        llm.generate(
+            prompts[:1], SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=8), use_tqdm=False
+        )
+        for mode, skip in (("recompute", True), ("prefix_cache", False)):
+            assert llm.reset_prefix_cache()
+            started = time.perf_counter()
+            outputs = llm.generate(
+                prompts,
+                SamplingParams(
+                    temperature=0,
+                    max_tokens=args.max_tokens,
+                    stop=["Question:", "Assistant:", "<|separator|>"],
+                    skip_reading_prefix_cache=skip,
+                ),
+                use_tqdm=False,
+            )
+            elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
+            rows = []
+            for index, output in zip(indices, outputs, strict=True):
+                assert output.prompt_token_ids is not None
+                completion = output.outputs[0]
+                predicted = answer_number(completion.text)
+                expected = answer_number(test[index]["answer"])
+                rows.append(
+                    {
+                        "index": index,
+                        "expected": expected,
+                        "predicted": predicted,
+                        "correct": expected is not None and predicted == expected,
+                        "text": completion.text,
+                        "token_ids": list(completion.token_ids),
+                        "finish_reason": completion.finish_reason,
+                        "prompt_tokens": len(output.prompt_token_ids),
+                        "cached_tokens": output.num_cached_tokens,
+                    }
+                )
+            accuracy = sum(row["correct"] for row in rows) / len(rows)
+            report["runs"][mode] = {
+                "seconds": elapsed,
+                "accuracy": accuracy,
+                "length_limited": sum(row["finish_reason"] == "length" for row in rows),
+                "rows": rows,
+            }
+            args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+            args.output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
+            print(
+                json.dumps(
+                    {
+                        "mode": mode,
+                        "samples": len(rows),
+                        "accuracy": accuracy,
+                        "length_limited": report["runs"][mode]["length_limited"],
+                        "cached_tokens": sum(row["cached_tokens"] or 0 for row in rows),
+                    }
+                ),
+                flush=True,
+            )
+        baseline, cached = report["runs"]["recompute"], report["runs"]["prefix_cache"]
+        report["answer_mismatches"] = sum(
+            a["predicted"] != b["predicted"]
+            for a, b in zip(baseline["rows"], cached["rows"], strict=True)
+        )
+        report["token_mismatches"] = sum(
+            a["token_ids"] != b["token_ids"]
+            for a, b in zip(baseline["rows"], cached["rows"], strict=True)
+        )
+        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        args.output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
+        assert all(not row["cached_tokens"] for row in baseline["rows"])
+        assert any(row["cached_tokens"] for row in cached["rows"])
+        assert baseline["length_limited"] <= 0.01 * args.num_samples
+        assert cached["length_limited"] <= 0.01 * args.num_samples
+        assert min(baseline["accuracy"], cached["accuracy"]) >= args.min_accuracy
+        assert baseline["accuracy"] - cached["accuracy"] <= args.max_accuracy_drop
+    finally:
+        llm.llm_engine.engine_core.shutdown()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""Validate attached and independent native KV movement against real servers."""

+

+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--base-url", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--engine-id")
+    parser.add_argument("--dataset", required=True, type=Path)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True, type=Path)

+    if args.destination_url and args.tier != "mooncake":
+        parser.error("Cross-engine preparation requires Mooncake")
+    if args.evaluation_samples < 0:
+        parser.error("--evaluation-samples must be nonnegative")
+    session = requests.Session()
+    base = args.base_url.rstrip("/")
+    run = uuid.uuid4().hex
+    report = {
+        "profile": "native_primitives",
+        "actions": {},
+        "inference": [],
+        "source_hashes": source_hashes(),
+        "dataset_identity": dataset_identity(args.dataset),

+
+    def get(path, base_url=base):

+        response.raise_for_status()
+        return response.json()
+
+    def post(path, payload, base_url=base):

+        return response.json()
+
+    engines = [
+        e
+        for e in get("/v1/kv/capabilities")["engines"]
+        if args.engine_id is None or e["engine_id"] == args.engine_id
+    ]
+    assert len(engines) == 1, engines
+    caps = engines[0]
+    report["capabilities"] = caps
+    invocation = {k: caps[k] for k in ("engine_id", "engine_epoch", "namespace")}
+
+    def control(method, payload):
+        return post(
+            "/v1/kv/control",
+            {"method": method, "invocation": invocation, "payload": payload},
+        )
+
+    def wait(name, *, acknowledge=True):
+        result = wait_operation(control, run + "-" + name, acknowledge=acknowledge)
+        report["actions"][name] = result
+        return result
+
+    model = get("/v1/models")["data"][0]["id"]
+    train = pq.read_table(
+        args.dataset / "main/train-00000-of-00001.parquet"
+    ).to_pylist()
+    text = "".join(
+        f"Question: {x['question']}\nAnswer: {x['answer']}\n\n" for x in train[:8]
+    )
+    text += "Question: What is 1 + 1?\nAnswer:"
+    tokens = post("/tokenize", {"model": model, "prompt": text})["tokens"]
+    boundary = math.lcm(
+        *(
+            g["block_size"]
+            for g in caps["cache_profile"]["groups"]
+            if g["prefix_cacheable"]
+        )
+    )
+    end = len(tokens) // boundary * boundary
+    assert end > 0
+    selector = {"kind": "request", "request_id": "$request", "end_token": end}
+
+    def infer(hints=None, *, base_url=base, model_id=None):
+        body = {
+            "model": model_id or model,
+            "prompt": tokens,
+            "temperature": 0,
+            "max_tokens": 16,
+            "return_token_ids": True,
+            "cache_salt": run,
+        }
+        if hints is not None:
+            body["kv_hints"] = hints
+        if args.tier == "cpu":
+            body["kv_transfer_params"] = {"max_load_tokens": 0}
+        response = post("/v1/completions", body, base_url)
+        report["inference"].append(response)
+        return response
+
+    report["passed"] = False
+    try:
+        first = infer(
+            envelope(
+                run + "-move",
+                "vllm.move_to",
+                {
+                    "target": selector,
+                    "src": {"tier": "gpu"},
+                    "dst": {"tier": args.tier},
+                },
+            )
+        )
+        moved = wait("move")
+        assert moved["status"] == "completed", moved
+        assert moved["target_outcomes"] and all(
+            "cold_copy_stored" in o["completed_steps"]
+            and "gpu_copies_reclaimed" in o["completed_steps"]
+            for o in moved["target_outcomes"]
+        ), moved
+        resumed = infer(
+            envelope(
+                run + "-copy",
+                "vllm.copy_to",
+                {
+                    "target": selector,
+                    "src": {"tier": args.tier},
+                    "dst": {"tier": "gpu"},
+                },
+            )
+        )
+        copied = wait("copy")
+        assert copied["status"] == "completed" and copied["target_outcomes"], copied
+        assert all(
+            o["transfer_id"] is not None
+            and "gpu_content_registered" in o["completed_steps"]
+            for o in copied["target_outcomes"]
+        ), copied
+        assert first["choices"][0]["token_ids"] == resumed["choices"][0]["token_ids"]
+        assert first["usage"]["prompt_tokens_details"]["cached_tokens"] == 0
+        assert resumed["usage"]["prompt_tokens_details"]["cached_tokens"] >= end
+        target = {
+            "kind": "hashes",
+            "namespace": caps["namespace"],
+            "blocks": [
+                {
+                    k: outcome[k]
+                    for k in ("block_hash", "group_id", "start_token", "end_token")
+                }
+                for outcome in copied["target_outcomes"]
+            ],
+        }
+
+        def action(name, kind, payload, *, acknowledge=True):
+            message = envelope(run + "-" + name, kind, payload)
+            control("submit", message)
+            result = wait(name, acknowledge=acknowledge)
+            assert result["status"] == "completed", result
+            return result
+
+        def movement(name, kind, source, destination):
+            return action(
+                name,
+                kind,
+                {
+                    "target": target,
+                    "src": {"tier": source},
+                    "dst": {"tier": destination},
+                },
+            )
+
+        priority = {
+            "target": target,
+            "location": "local_g1",
+            "claim_id": run,
+            "revision": 1,
+            "value": 80,
+            "ttl_seconds": 300,
+        }
+        action("priority", "vllm.set_priority", priority, acknowledge=False)
+        assert control(
+            "submit", envelope(run + "-priority", "vllm.set_priority", priority)
+        )["replayed"]
+        control("acknowledge", {"message_id": run + "-priority"})
+        replay = session.post(
+            base + "/v1/kv/control",
+            json={
+                "method": "submit",
+                "invocation": invocation,
+                "payload": envelope(run + "-priority", "vllm.set_priority", priority),
+            },
+            timeout=30,
+        )
+        assert replay.status_code == 409 and replay.json()["error"]["code"] == (
+            "acknowledged"
+        )
+        report["acknowledged_replay"] = replay.json()
+        action(
+            "release",
+            "vllm.set_priority",
+            {
+                **priority,
+                "revision": 2,
+                "value": None,
+                "ttl_seconds": None,
+            },
+        )
+        movement("independent-copy", "vllm.copy_to", "gpu", args.tier)
+        assert cached(infer()) >= end
+        movement("independent-move", "vllm.move_to", "gpu", args.tier)
+        movement("independent-prepare", "vllm.copy_to", args.tier, "gpu")
+        again = infer()
+        assert cached(again) >= end
+        assert again["choices"][0]["token_ids"] == first["choices"][0]["token_ids"]
+
+        if args.destination_url:
+            (peer,) = get("/v1/kv/capabilities", args.destination_url)["engines"]
+            assert peer["namespace"] == caps["namespace"], (caps, peer)
+            assert peer["engine_id"] != caps["engine_id"]
+            assert peer["engine_epoch"] != caps["engine_epoch"]
+
+            def peer_control(method, payload):
+                return post(
+                    "/v1/kv/control",
+                    {
+                        "method": method,
+                        "invocation": {k: peer[k] for k in invocation},
+                        "payload": payload,
+                    },
+                    args.destination_url,
+                )
+
+            message = run + "-peer-copy"
+            peer_control(
+                "submit",
+                envelope(
+                    message,
+                    "vllm.copy_to",
+                    {
+                        "target": target,
+                        "src": {"tier": "mooncake"},
+                        "dst": {"tier": "gpu"},
+                    },
+                ),
+            )
+            ready = wait_operation(peer_control, message, acknowledge=True)
+            assert ready["status"] == "completed", ready
+            peer_model = get("/v1/models", args.destination_url)["data"][0]["id"]
+            response = infer(base_url=args.destination_url, model_id=peer_model)
+            assert cached(response) >= end
+            assert (
+                response["choices"][0]["token_ids"] == first["choices"][0]["token_ids"]
+            )
+            report["cross_engine"] = {"destination": peer, "readiness": ready}
+
+        if args.policy:
+            for name, signal in (
+                ("policy-move", "tool_wait"),
+                ("policy-copy", "resume"),
+            ):
+                receipt = control(
+                    "submit",
+                    envelope(
+                        run + "-" + name,
+                        "signal",
+                        {"target": target, "signal": signal},
+                        "1",
+                    ),
+                )
+                parent = receipt["results"][0]
+                assert (
+                    parent["status"] == "completed" and parent["derived_operations"]
+                ), parent
+                children = [
+                    wait_operation(
+                        control,
+                        child["message_id"],
+                        child["action_id"],
+                        acknowledge=True,
+                    )
+                    for child in parent["derived_operations"]
+                ]
+                assert all(child["status"] == "completed" for child in children), (
+                    children
+                )
+                report["actions"][name] = {"parent": parent, "children": children}
+                control("acknowledge", {"message_id": parent["message_id"]})
+            again = infer()
+            assert again["usage"]["prompt_tokens_details"]["cached_tokens"] >= end
+            assert again["choices"][0]["token_ids"] == first["choices"][0]["token_ids"]
+        if args.evaluation_samples:
+            test = pq.read_table(
+                args.dataset / "main/test-00000-of-00001.parquet"
+            ).to_pylist()
+            assert 0 < args.evaluation_samples <= len(test)
+            indices = random.Random(0).sample(range(len(test)), args.evaluation_samples)
+            shared_text = "".join(
+                f"Question: {x['question']}\nAnswer: {x['answer']}\n\n"
+                for x in train[:8]

+
+            def evaluate_question(index, mode):
+                body = {
+                    "model": model,
+                    "prompt": shared_text
+                    + f"Question: {test[index]['question']}\nAnswer:",
+                    "temperature": 0,
+                    "max_tokens": 1024,
+                    "stop": ["Question:", "Assistant:", "<|separator|>"],
+                    "return_token_ids": True,
+                }
+                body["cache_salt"] = (
+                    f"{run}-question-{index}" if mode == "recompute" else run
+                )
+                if args.tier == "cpu":
+                    body["kv_transfer_params"] = {"max_load_tokens": 0}
+                response = requests.post(
+                    args.base_url + "/v1/completions",
+                    json=body,
+                    timeout=600,
+                )
+                response.raise_for_status()
+                output = response.json()
+                choice = output["choices"][0]
+                expected = answer_number(test[index]["answer"])
+                predicted = answer_number(choice["text"])
+                return {
+                    "index": index,
+                    "expected": expected,
+                    "predicted": predicted,
+                    "correct": expected is not None and predicted == expected,
+                    "text": choice["text"],
+                    "token_ids": choice["token_ids"],
+                    "finish_reason": choice["finish_reason"],
+                    "cached_tokens": cached(output),
+                }
+
+            evaluation = {"indices": indices, "seed": 0, "num_fewshot": 8, "runs": {}}
+            report["evaluation"] = evaluation
+            for mode in (
+                "recompute",
+                "prepared",
+            ):
+                rows = []
+                started = time.perf_counter()
+                with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as workers:
+                    for offset in range(0, len(indices), 8):
+                        if mode == "prepared":
+                            infer()
+                            name = f"evaluation-demote-{offset}"
+                            movement(name, "vllm.move_to", "gpu", args.tier)
+                            movement(
+                                f"evaluation-copy-{offset}",
+                                "vllm.copy_to",
+                                args.tier,
+                                "gpu",
+                            )
+                        rows.extend(
+                            workers.map(
+                                lambda index, mode=mode: evaluate_question(index, mode),
+                                indices[offset : offset + 8],
+                            )
+                        )
+                result = {
+                    "seconds": time.perf_counter() - started,
+                    "accuracy": sum(r["correct"] for r in rows) / len(rows),
+                    "length_limited": sum(r["finish_reason"] == "length" for r in rows),
+                    "rows": rows,
+                }
+                evaluation["runs"][mode] = result
+                args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+                args.output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
+                print(
+                    json.dumps(
+                        {
+                            "mode": mode,
+                            "accuracy": result["accuracy"],
+                            "samples": len(rows),
+                        }
+                    ),
+                    flush=True,
+                )
+            baseline, moved = evaluation["runs"].values()
+            assert all(row["cached_tokens"] == 0 for row in baseline["rows"])
+            prefix_tokens = post("/tokenize", {"model": model, "prompt": shared_text})[
+                "tokens"
+            ]
+            reusable = len(prefix_tokens) // boundary * boundary
+            assert reusable > 0
+            assert all(row["cached_tokens"] >= reusable for row in moved["rows"])
+            assert baseline["length_limited"] <= 0.01 * args.evaluation_samples

+            assert min(baseline["accuracy"], moved["accuracy"]) >= 0.8

+        report["final_capacity"] = control("capacity", {})

+        report["passed"] = True
+    except Exception as error:
+        report["error"] = str(error)
+        raise
+    finally:
+        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        args.output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
+        session.close()
+    print(
+        json.dumps(
+            {
+                "passed": True,
+                "cached_tokens": resumed["usage"]["prompt_tokens_details"][
+                    "cached_tokens"
+                ],
+            }
+        )
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Real shared branches, independent TTLs, resume races and cancellation."""
+
+import argparse
+import asyncio
+import gzip
+import json
+import uuid
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from benchmarks.programmable_kv_cache.client import envelope
+from benchmarks.programmable_kv_cache.rollout import RolloutClient
+from benchmarks.programmable_kv_cache.run_rollout_matrix import source_hashes
+
+
+async def run(args):
+    client = RolloutClient(args.base_url, "priority")
+    report = {
+        "passed": False,
+        "requests": client.rows,
+        "controls": client.controls,
+        "source_hashes": source_hashes(),
+    }
+    try:
+        await client.initialize()
+        with gzip.open(args.trace, "rt") as file:
+            prompt = json.load(file)["requests"][0]["prompt_ids"]
+        prompt = prompt[: client.boundary + 128]
+        root = await client.generate(
+            "root", prompt, {"temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 16}
+        )
+        root_target = client.targets["root"]
+        parent = {
+            "session_id": root_target["session_id"],
+            "continuation_id": "turn-0",
+            "end_token": client.boundary,
+        }
+        for name, tail in (("b", "Branch B"), ("c", "Branch C")):
+            response = await client.http.post(
+                "/tokenize", json={"model": client.model, "prompt": tail}
+            )
+            response.raise_for_status()
+            branch = await client.generate(
+                name,
+                prompt + root["token_ids"] + response.json()["tokens"],
+                {"temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 16},
+                task_parent_id=root_target["session_id"],
+                parent_prefix=parent,
+            )
+            assert (
+                branch["usage"]["prompt_tokens_details"]["cached_tokens"]
+                >= client.boundary
+            )
+        shared = await client.generate(
+            "external", prompt, {"temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 16}
+        )
+        assert (
+            shared["usage"]["prompt_tokens_details"]["cached_tokens"] >= client.boundary
+        )
+        external = client.targets["external"]
+        residency = await client.call("residency", {"target": external})
+        blocks = [
+            {
+                key: row[key]
+                for key in ("block_hash", "group_id", "start_token", "end_token")
+            }
+            for row in residency["items"]
+            if row["resident_copies"]
+        ]
+        assert blocks
+        target = {
+            "kind": "hashes",
+            "namespace": client.invocation["namespace"],
+            "blocks": blocks,
+            "start_token": 0,
+            "end_token": client.boundary,
+        }
+        for owner, priority, ttl in (
+            (root_target["session_id"], 90, 60),
+            (external["session_id"], 20, 2),
+        ):
+            result = await client.action(
+                "retain",
+                {
+                    "target": target,
+                    "owner_id": owner,
+                    "declaration_id": "shared",
+                    "priority": priority,
+                    "ttl_seconds": ttl,
+                },
+                version="1",
+            )
+            assert result["status"] == "completed", result
+
+        async def priorities():
+            current = await client.call("residency", {"target": target})
+            report.setdefault("residency", []).append(current)
+            return {p for row in current["items"] for p in row["eviction_priorities"]}
+
+        assert await priorities() == {90}
+        await client.finish("root")
+        snapshot = await client.call("associations", {})
+        report["after_task_tree_cleanup"] = snapshot
+        names = {row["session_id"] for row in snapshot["items"]}
+        assert external["session_id"] in names
+        assert root_target["session_id"] not in names
+        assert client.targets["b"]["session_id"] not in names
+        assert client.targets["c"]["session_id"] not in names
+        assert await priorities() == {20}
+        await asyncio.sleep(2.1)
+        assert await priorities() == {0}
+
+        stored = await client.action(
+            "vllm.copy_to",
+            {
+                "target": target,
+                "src": {"tier": "gpu"},
+                "dst": {"tier": "mooncake"},
+            },
+        )
+        assert stored["status"] == "completed", stored
+        evicted = await client.action("evict", {"target": target}, version="1")
+        assert evicted["status"] == "completed", evicted
+        if args.capacity_deferral:
+            payload = {
+                "target": target,
+                "src": {"tier": "mooncake"},
+                "dst": {"tier": "gpu"},
+            }
+            attempts = []
+            for _ in range(len(blocks) + 1):
+                result = await client.action("vllm.copy_to", payload)
+                attempts.append(result)
+                if result["status"] == "completed":
+                    break
+                assert result["status"] == "partial" and result["blocked_targets"] > 0
+            assert attempts[0]["status"] == "partial"
+            assert attempts[-1]["status"] == "completed"
+            report["capacity_retry"] = attempts
+            resumed = await client.generate(
+                "capacity-resumed", prompt, {"temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 16}
+            )
+            assert (
+                resumed["usage"]["prompt_tokens_details"]["cached_tokens"]
+                >= client.boundary
+            )
+            assert resumed["token_ids"] == root["token_ids"]
+            await client.action("evict", {"target": target}, version="1")
+            partial = await client.action("vllm.copy_to", payload)
+            assert partial["status"] == "partial" and partial["blocked_targets"] > 0
+            fallback = await client.generate(
+                "capacity-fallback", prompt, {"temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 16}
+            )
+            assert fallback["usage"]["prompt_tokens_details"]["cached_tokens"] == 0
+            assert fallback["token_ids"] == root["token_ids"]
+            report["capacity_fallback"] = partial
+            for identifier in tuple(client.targets):
+                await client.finish(identifier)
+            report["final_capacity"] = await client.wait_control_idle()
+            report["final_associations"] = await client.call("associations", {})
+            assert report["final_capacity"]["records"] == 0
+            assert not report["final_associations"]["items"]
+            report["passed"] = True
+            return
+        message = uuid.uuid4().hex
+        command = envelope(
+            message,
+            "vllm.copy_to",
+            {
+                "target": target,
+                "src": {"tier": "mooncake"},
+                "dst": {"tier": "gpu"},
+            },
+        )
+        submitted = await client.call("submit", command)
+        assert (await client.call("submit", command))["replayed"]
+        resumed = await client.generate(
+            "raced", prompt, {"temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 16}
+        )
+        prepared = await client.wait(message)
+        assert prepared["status"] == "completed"
+        assert (
+            resumed["usage"]["prompt_tokens_details"]["cached_tokens"]
+            >= client.boundary
+        )
+        assert resumed["token_ids"] == root["token_ids"]
+        report["resume_race"] = {"submission": submitted, "completion": prepared}
+
+        await client.action("evict", {"target": target}, version="1")
+        message = uuid.uuid4().hex
+        receipt = await client.call(
+            "submit",
+            envelope(
+                message,
+                "vllm.copy_to",
+                {
+                    "target": target,
+                    "src": {"tier": "mooncake"},
+                    "dst": {"tier": "gpu"},
+                },
+            ),
+        )
+        operation = receipt["results"][0]
+        cancelled = await client.call(
+            "cancel",
+            {
+                key: operation[key]
+                for key in ("message_id", "action_id", "operation_id")
+            },
+        )
+        assert cancelled["status"] in ("cancelled", "completed"), cancelled
+        report["cancellation"] = cancelled
+        await client.wait(message)
+        fallback = await client.generate(
+            "fallback", prompt, {"temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 16}
+        )
+        assert fallback["token_ids"] == root["token_ids"]
+        absent = dict(target, blocks=[dict(b, block_hash="ff" * 32) for b in blocks])
+        missing = await client.action(
+            "vllm.copy_to",
+            {
+                "target": absent,
+                "src": {"tier": "mooncake"},
+                "dst": {"tier": "gpu"},
+            },
+        )
+        assert missing["status"] == "missing", missing
+        report["missing_content"] = missing
+        for identifier in tuple(client.targets):
+            await client.finish(identifier)
+        report["final_capacity"] = await client.wait_control_idle()
+        report["final_associations"] = await client.call("associations", {})
+        assert report["final_capacity"]["records"] == 0
+        assert not report["final_associations"]["items"]
+        report["passed"] = True
+        print(
+            json.dumps({"passed": True, "branches": 3, "shared_priority": [90, 20, 0]})
+        )
+    except BaseException as error:
+        report["error"] = f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"
+        raise
+    finally:
+        try:
+            await client.close()
+        finally:
+            args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+            with gzip.open(args.output, "wt") as file:
+                json.dump(report, file)
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--base-url", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--trace", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--capacity-deferral",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="Check partial loads and retry on a server with a one-block load budget",
+    )
+    asyncio.run(run(parser.parse_args()))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""Opt-in profiling bootstrap, added to server PYTHONPATH by the benchmark."""
+
+import faulthandler
+import importlib
+import json
+import os
+import signal
+import threading
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+
+if directory := os.environ.get("KV_BENCH_CPU_PROFILE_DIR"):
+    root = Path(directory)
+    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    pid = os.getpid()
+    stat = Path(f"/proc/{pid}/stat").read_text()
+    start_ticks = int(stat[stat.rfind(")") + 2 :].split()[19])
+    metadata = root / f"{pid}.json"
+    profile = importlib.import_module("yappi")
+    profile.set_clock_type("cpu")
+    active = False
+    profiled_threads = []
+    cpu_started = cpu_seconds = None
+
+    def record(state):
+        threads = {t.native_id: t.name for t in threading.enumerate()}
+        temporary = metadata.with_suffix(".tmp")
+        temporary.write_text(
+            json.dumps(

+class ToolDurationEstimator:
+    """Estimate a tool batch using only previously completed batches."""
+
+    def __init__(self, initial_seconds: float, max_batches: int = 64):
+        if not math.isfinite(initial_seconds) or initial_seconds <= 0:
+            raise ValueError("Initial tool duration must be positive and finite")
+        if max_batches < 1:
+            raise ValueError("Tool batch history must be positive")
+        self.initial_seconds = initial_seconds
+        self.max_batches = max_batches
+        self.history: OrderedDict[tuple[str, ...], float] = OrderedDict()
+
+    def predict(self, tools: tuple[str, ...]) -> float:
+        return self.history.get(tuple(sorted(tools)), self.initial_seconds)
+
+    def observe(self, tools: tuple[str, ...], seconds: float) -> None:
+        if not math.isfinite(seconds) or seconds < 0:
+            raise ValueError("Observed tool duration must be nonnegative and finite")
+        key = tuple(sorted(tools))
+        previous = self.history.get(key, seconds)
+        self.history[key] = max(0.001, 0.75 * previous + 0.25 * seconds)
+        self.history.move_to_end(key)
+        while len(self.history) > self.max_batches:
+            self.history.popitem(last=False)

+"""Run isolated, repeated serving comparisons; only use explicitly selected GPUs."""
+
+import argparse
+import csv
+import gzip
+import hashlib
+import importlib.metadata
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import math
+import os

+import random

+import requests
+
+
+def install_signal_handlers():
+    def interrupted(signum, frame):
+        raise KeyboardInterrupt(f"Received signal {signum}")
+
+    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, signal.default_int_handler)
+    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, interrupted)
+
+
+def stop(process, *, interrupt=False):
+    if process is None or process.poll() is not None:
+        return
+    try:
+        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGINT if interrupt else signal.SIGTERM)
+        process.wait(timeout=45)
+    except ProcessLookupError:
+        pass
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+        process.wait(timeout=15)
+
+
+def require_free_port(port):
+    try:
+        connection = socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port), timeout=1)
+    except OSError:
+        return
+    connection.close()
+    raise RuntimeError(f"Port {port} already belongs to another process")
+
+
+def reset_cache(base, controlled):
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + 120
+    while True:
+        reset = requests.post(
+            base + "/reset_prefix_cache",
+            params={"reset_external": controlled},
+            timeout=120,
+        )
+        reset.raise_for_status()
+        if reset.json()["success"]:
+            return
+        if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
+            raise RuntimeError("Cache reset remained busy")
+        time.sleep(1)
+
+
+def source_hashes():
+    names = subprocess.check_output(
+        ["git", "diff", "--name-only"], text=True
+    ).splitlines()
+    names.extend(str(p) for p in Path("benchmarks/programmable_kv_cache").glob("*.py"))
+    names.extend(
+        str(p)
+        for p in Path("benchmarks/programmable_kv_cache/profile_bootstrap").glob("*.py")
+    )
+    return {
+        name: hashlib.sha256(Path(name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+        for name in sorted(set(names))
+        if Path(name).is_file()
+    }
+
+
+def dataset_identity(directory):
+    metadata = (
+        directory
+        / ".cache/huggingface/download/main/test-00000-of-00001.parquet.metadata"
+    )
+    return {
+        "revision": metadata.read_text().splitlines()[0] if metadata.exists() else None,
+        "sha256": {
+            str(path.relative_to(directory)): hashlib.sha256(
+                path.read_bytes()
+            ).hexdigest()
+            for path in sorted((directory / "main").glob("*.parquet"))
+        },
+    }
+
+
+def read_cpu_stat(path):
+    stat = path.read_text()
+    end = stat.rfind(")")
+    values = stat[end + 2 :].split()
+    return {
+        "name": stat[stat.index("(") + 1 : end],
+        "start_ticks": int(values[19]),
+        "cpu_seconds": (int(values[11]) + int(values[12])) / os.sysconf("SC_CLK_TCK"),
+    }
+
+
+def process_cpu(root_pid):
+    parents = {}
+    for line in subprocess.check_output(
+        ["ps", "-e", "-o", "pid=,ppid="], text=True
+    ).splitlines():
+        pid, parent = map(int, line.split())
+        parents.setdefault(parent, []).append(pid)
+    pending, result = [root_pid], {}
+    while pending:
+        pid = pending.pop()
+        pending.extend(parents.get(pid, []))
+        try:
+            result[pid] = read_cpu_stat(Path(f"/proc/{pid}/stat"))
+        except (FileNotFoundError, ProcessLookupError):
+            continue
+        threads = result[pid]["threads"] = {}
+        for path in Path(f"/proc/{pid}/task").glob("*/stat"):
+            try:
+                threads[int(path.parent.name)] = read_cpu_stat(path)
+            except (FileNotFoundError, ProcessLookupError):
+                continue
+    return result
+
+
+def toggle_cpu_profiles(directory, processes, expected, *, strict=True):
+    for pid, identity in processes.items():
+        try:
+            metadata = json.loads((directory / f"{pid}.json").read_text())
+            current = Path(f"/proc/{pid}/stat").read_text()
+            start = int(current[current.rfind(")") + 2 :].split()[19])
+            if (
+                start != identity["start_ticks"]
+                or start != metadata["start_ticks"]
+                or metadata["state"] != expected
+            ):
+                raise RuntimeError(f"Unexpected CPU profiler state: {metadata}")
+            os.kill(pid, signal.SIGUSR2)
+        except (OSError, RuntimeError):
+            if strict:
+                raise
+
+
+def wait_cpu_profiles(directory, processes, expected):
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + 15
+    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+        if all(
+            json.loads((directory / f"{pid}.json").read_text())["state"] == expected
+            for pid in processes
+        ):
+            return
+        time.sleep(0.05)
+    raise TimeoutError(f"CPU profilers did not reach {expected}")
+
+
+def gpu_process_window(path, start, finish, owned_pids):
+    with path.open() as file:
+        lines = file.readlines()
+    if lines and not lines[-1].endswith("\n"):
+        lines.pop()
+    devices, unexpected = {}, {}
+    for row in csv.DictReader(lines, skipinitialspace=True):
+        timestamp = datetime.strptime(row["timestamp"], "%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%S.%f")
+        epoch = timestamp.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc).timestamp()
+        if not start <= epoch <= finish:
+            continue
+        device, pid = row["gpu_uuid"], int(row["pid"])
+        devices.setdefault(device, set()).add(epoch)
+        if pid not in owned_pids:
+            key = device, pid
+            entry = unexpected.setdefault(
+                key,
+                {
+                    "gpu_uuid": device,
+                    "pid": pid,
+                    "process_name": row["process_name"],
+                    "first_epoch": epoch,
+                    "last_epoch": epoch,
+                },
+            )
+            entry["last_epoch"] = epoch
+    coverage = {}
+    for device, timestamps in devices.items():
+        times = sorted(timestamps)
+        coverage[device] = {
+            "samples": len(times),
+            "max_gap_seconds": max(
+                b - a for a, b in zip([start, *times], [*times, finish])
+            ),
+        }
+    return {"devices": coverage, "unexpected_processes": list(unexpected.values())}
+
+

+    if audit["unexpected_processes"]:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"GPU sharing invalidates this run: {audit}")
+    if len(audit["devices"]) != expected_devices or any(
+        device["max_gap_seconds"] > 10 for device in audit["devices"].values()
+    ):
+        raise RuntimeError(f"GPU process log coverage incomplete: {audit}")
+
+

+def arithmetic(expression: str) -> str:
+    """Evaluate bounded arithmetic supplied by an actual model tool call."""
+    operations = {
+        ast.Add: operator.add,
+        ast.Sub: operator.sub,
+        ast.Mult: operator.mul,
+        ast.Div: operator.truediv,
+        ast.FloorDiv: operator.floordiv,
+        ast.Mod: operator.mod,
+    }
+    if len(expression) > 512:
+        raise ValueError("Expression is too long")
+
+    def visit(node):
+        if (
+            isinstance(node, ast.Constant)
+            and type(node.value) in (int, float)
+            and abs(node.value) <= 1e12
+        ):
+            return node.value
+        if isinstance(node, ast.UnaryOp) and isinstance(node.op, (ast.UAdd, ast.USub)):
+            value = visit(node.operand)
+            return -value if isinstance(node.op, ast.USub) else value
+        if isinstance(node, ast.BinOp) and type(node.op) in operations:
+            value = operations[type(node.op)](visit(node.left), visit(node.right))
+            if abs(value) <= 1e15:
+                return value
+        raise ValueError("Use only numeric constants and basic arithmetic")
+
+    return str(visit(ast.parse(expression, mode="eval").body))

+def percentile(values, fraction):
