+    }
+
+    async def episode(identifier, rows):
+        rows.sort(key=lambda r: r["turn"])
+        queued = time.perf_counter()
+        async with semaphore:
+            started = time.perf_counter()
+            for turn, row in enumerate(rows):
+                if turn:
+                    pause = max(
+                        args.replay_pause_floor,
+                        row["started"] - rows[turn - 1]["finished"],
+                    )
+                    names = tool_names.get((identifier, turn - 1), ("recorded_tool",))
+                    predicted = (
+                        pause
+                        if args.oracle
+                        else estimator.predict(names)
+                        if args.prediction_mode == "adaptive"
+                        else args.prediction_seconds
+                    )
+                    await client.pause(identifier, predicted)
+                    pause_started = time.monotonic()
+                    await asyncio.sleep(pause)
+                    elapsed = time.monotonic() - pause_started
+                    estimator.observe(names, elapsed)
+                    report["tool_waits"].append(
+                        {
+                            "request_id": identifier,
+                            "turn": turn - 1,
+                            "tools": names,
+                            "predicted_seconds": predicted,
+                            "actual_seconds": elapsed,
+                        }
+                    )
+                generated = await client.generate(
+                    identifier,
+                    row["prompt_ids"],
+                    {"temperature": 0},
+                    fixed_tokens=len(row["token_ids"]),
+                )
+                assert len(generated["token_ids"]) == len(row["token_ids"])
+            await client.finish(identifier)
+            report["episodes"].append(
+                {
+                    **{
+                        k: v
+                        for k, v in episode_metadata[identifier].items()
+                        if k in ("family", "index", "sample")
+                    },
+                    "request_id": identifier,
+                    "seconds": time.perf_counter() - started,
+                    "client_queue_seconds": started - queued,
+                    "num_turns": len(rows),
+                }
+            )
+            if len(report["episodes"]) % 32 == 0:
+                print(
+                    json.dumps({"completed_rollouts": len(report["episodes"])}),
+                    flush=True,
+                )
+
+    report["workload_started"] = time.perf_counter()
+    report["workload_cpu_started"] = time.process_time()
+    await run_episodes(episode(key, rows) for key, rows in trajectories.items())
+
+
+async def run(args):
+    client = RolloutClient(
+        args.base_url,
+        args.mode,
+        seed=args.seed,
+        trace_rpc=args.trace_control_rpc,
+        control_timeout=args.control_timeout,
+    )
+    report = {
+        "clock": {"wall_time": time.time(), "monotonic": time.perf_counter()},
+        "config": {
+            k: str(v) if isinstance(v, Path) else v for k, v in vars(args).items()
+        },
+        "requests": client.rows,
+        "controls": client.controls,
+        "control_rpc": client.rpc_stats,
+        "control_rpc_requests": client.rpc_rows,
+        "episodes": [],
+        "tool_waits": [],
+        "passed": False,
+        "source_revision": subprocess.check_output(
+            ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True
+        ).strip(),
+        "source_hashes": source_hashes(),
+        "dataset_identity": dataset_identity(args.dataset),
+        "driver_sha256": hashlib.sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
+        "cache_salt": client.run_id,
+    }
+    stop = asyncio.Event()
+    sampler = None
+    try:
+        await client.initialize()
+        report["capabilities"] = client.capabilities
+        if client.invocation:
+            report["control_before"] = await client.call("capacity", {})
+        sampler = asyncio.create_task(metrics(client, report, stop))
+        started = time.perf_counter()
+        if args.trace:
+            await replay(args, client, report)
+        else:
+            await live(args, client, report)
+        if client.invocation:
+            report["control_capacity"] = await client.wait_control_idle()
+        report["seconds"] = time.perf_counter() - report.get(
+            "workload_started", started
+        )
+        report["driver_cpu_seconds"] = (
+            time.process_time() - report["workload_cpu_started"]
+        )
+        response = await client.http.get("/metrics")
+        response.raise_for_status()
+        report["metrics_after"] = response.text
+        if client.invocation:
+            assert not report["control_capacity"].get("policy_errors"), report[
+                "control_capacity"
+            ]
+            assert not report["control_capacity"]["records"], report["control_capacity"]
+            assert not any(r["status"] == "client_error" for r in client.controls)
+            report["logical_after"] = await client.call("associations", {})
+            assert not report["logical_after"]["items"], report["logical_after"]
+        report["summary"] = summarize(report)
+        report["passed"] = True
+        print(json.dumps(report["summary"]), flush=True)
+    except BaseException as error:
+        report["error"] = f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"
+        raise
+    finally:
+        stop.set()
+        if sampler is not None:
+            try:
+                await sampler
+            except Exception as error:
+                report["metrics_error"] = str(error)
+                report["passed"] = False
+        try:
+            await client.close()
+        except Exception as error:
+            report["cleanup_error"] = str(error)
+            report["passed"] = False
+        finally:
+            args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+            with gzip.open(args.output, "wt") as file:
+                json.dump(report, file)
+    if not report["passed"]:
+        raise RuntimeError("Benchmark cleanup or metrics collection failed")
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--base-url", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--model", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--dataset", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--verl-root", type=Path, default=Path("../verl"))
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)

+    parser.add_argument("--families", type=int, default=4)
+    parser.add_argument("--fewshot", type=int, default=24)
+    parser.add_argument("--concurrency", type=int, default=16)

+    parser.add_argument(

+    if args.replay_pause_floor and not args.trace:

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""Change real Qwen weights through CUDA IPC while old KV remains in the Store."""
+
+import argparse
+import asyncio
+import gzip
+import hashlib
+import json
+from dataclasses import asdict
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+from safetensors import safe_open
+from torch.multiprocessing.reductions import reduce_tensor
+
+from benchmarks.programmable_kv_cache.rollout import RolloutClient
+from benchmarks.programmable_kv_cache.run_rollout_matrix import source_hashes
+from vllm.distributed.weight_transfer.clients import HTTPVLLMWeightSyncClient
+from vllm.distributed.weight_transfer.ipc_engine import IPCWeightTransferUpdateInfo
+
+
+async def run(args):
+    client = RolloutClient(args.base_url, "priority")
+    report = {
+        "passed": False,
+        "requests": client.rows,
+        "controls": client.controls,
+        "scope": "real single-parameter IPC update and rollback; no optimizer step",
+        "source_hashes": source_hashes(),
+    }
+    sync = HTTPVLLMWeightSyncClient(args.base_url)
+    with gzip.open(args.trace, "rt") as file:
+        prompt = json.load(file)["requests"][0]["prompt_ids"]
+    index = json.loads((args.model / "model.safetensors.index.json").read_text())
+    name = next(
+        n for n in index["weight_map"] if n.endswith("layers.0.input_layernorm.weight")
+    )
+    with safe_open(args.model / index["weight_map"][name], framework="pt") as file:
+        original = file.get_tensor(name)
+    changed = original + 0.125
+    report["parameter"] = name
+    report["original_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(
+        original.view(torch.uint8).numpy()
+    ).hexdigest()
+    report["changed_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(
+        changed.view(torch.uint8).numpy()
+    ).hexdigest()
+
+    async def update(tensor, version):
+        for identifier in tuple(client.background):
+            await client.drain(identifier)
+        response = await client.http.post(
+            "/pause", params={"mode": "wait", "clear_cache": False}
+        )
+        response.raise_for_status()
+        await asyncio.to_thread(sync.start_weight_update)
+        copies, handles = [], {}
+        for device in range(torch.accelerator.device_count()):
+            copy = tensor.to(device=f"cuda:{device}").contiguous()
+            torch.accelerator.synchronize(device)
+            copies.append(copy)
+            handles[str(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device).uuid)] = reduce_tensor(
+                copy
+            )[1]
+        payload = IPCWeightTransferUpdateInfo(
+            names=[name],
+            dtype_names=[str(tensor.dtype).removeprefix("torch.")],
+            shapes=[list(tensor.shape)],
+            ipc_handles=[handles],
+        )
+        await asyncio.to_thread(sync.update_weights, asdict(payload))
+        await asyncio.to_thread(sync.finish_weight_update, version)
+        response = await client.http.post("/resume")
+        response.raise_for_status()
+        await client.initialize()
+        return list(copies)
+
+    try:
+        await client.initialize()
+        prompt = prompt[: client.boundary + 128]
+        report["input_tokens"] = len(prompt)
+        before_caps = client.capabilities
+        before_version = (await client.http.get("/weight_info")).json()[
+            "weight_version"
+        ]
+        report["before_weight_version"] = before_version
+        before = await client.generate(
+            "weight-before", prompt, {"temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 32}
+        )
+        logical = client.targets["weight-before"]
+        resident = await client.call("residency", {"target": logical, "limit": 4096})
+        target = {
+            "kind": "hashes",
+            "namespace": client.invocation["namespace"],
+            "blocks": [
+                {
+                    k: row[k]
+                    for k in ("block_hash", "group_id", "start_token", "end_token")
+                }
+                for row in resident["items"]
+                if row["resident_copies"]
+            ],
+        }
+        assert target["blocks"]
+        stored = await client.action(
+            "vllm.copy_to",
+            {
+                "target": target,
+                "src": {"tier": "gpu"},
+                "dst": {"tier": "mooncake"},
+            },
+        )
+        assert stored["status"] == "completed", stored
+        old_context = dict(client.invocation)
+        await asyncio.to_thread(sync.init_weight_transfer_engine, {"packed": False})
+        refs = await update(changed, "rollout-weights-changed")
+        report["changed_capabilities"] = client.capabilities
+        assert client.invocation["namespace"] != old_context["namespace"]
+        stale = await client.http.post(
+            "/v1/kv/control",
+            json={
+                "method": "associations",
+                "invocation": old_context,
+                "payload": {},
+            },
+        )
+        assert stale.status_code == 409, stale.text
+        report["stale_epoch"] = stale.json()
+        incompatible = await client.http.post(
+            "/v1/kv/control",
+            json={
+                "method": "residency",
+                "invocation": client.invocation,
+                "payload": {"target": target},
+            },
+        )
+        assert incompatible.json()["error"]["code"] == "incompatible"
+        relabeled = dict(target, namespace=client.invocation["namespace"])
+        missing = await client.action(
+            "vllm.copy_to",
+            {
+                "target": relabeled,
+                "src": {"tier": "mooncake"},
+                "dst": {"tier": "gpu"},
+            },
+        )
+        assert missing["status"] == "missing", missing
+        changed_output = await client.generate(
+            "weight-changed", prompt, {"temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 32}
+        )
+        assert changed_output["usage"]["prompt_tokens_details"]["cached_tokens"] == 0
+        assert before["log_probs"] != changed_output["log_probs"]
+        del refs
+        refs = await update(original, before_version)
+        assert client.invocation["namespace"] == before_caps["namespace"]
+        recovered = await client.action(
+            "vllm.copy_to",
+            {
+                "target": target,
+                "src": {"tier": "mooncake"},
+                "dst": {"tier": "gpu"},
+            },
+        )
+        assert recovered["status"] == "completed", recovered
+        assert all(
+            row["transfer_id"] is not None for row in recovered["target_outcomes"]
+        )
+        restored = await client.generate(
+            "weight-restored", prompt, {"temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 32}
+        )
+        assert restored["token_ids"] == before["token_ids"]
+        assert restored["usage"]["prompt_tokens_details"]["cached_tokens"] > 0
+        report["passed"] = True
+        report["old_store_objects_survived"] = True
+        del refs
+        print(
+            json.dumps(
+                {"passed": True, "parameter": name, "old_store_objects_survived": True}
+            ),
+            flush=True,
+        )
+    except BaseException as error:
+        report["error"] = f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"
+        raise
+    finally:
+        await client.close()
+        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        with gzip.open(args.output, "wt") as file:
+            json.dump(report, file)
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--base-url", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--model", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--trace", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
+    asyncio.run(run(parser.parse_args()))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+        async def kv_control(self, method, invocation, payload):

+def hint(message, kind, payload):

+def test_http_submission_and_python_query_share_results_and_retries(control_client):

+        "replayed"

+class QueuedControlTransfers:
+    tier = "mooncake"
+    actions = ("prefetch", "demote", "share")
+    limitations = ()
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.jobs = []
+        self.completions = []
+
+    def validate(self, direction, key, num_tokens):
+        pass
+
+    def submit(self, lease):
+        self.jobs.append(lease)
+
+    def poll(self):
+        result, self.completions = tuple(self.completions), []
+        return result
+
+    def finish(self, success=True, *, bytes_transferred=0):
+        self.completions.extend(
+            KVTransferCompletion(
+                job.transfer_id,
+                job.generation,
+                success,
+                bytes_transferred=bytes_transferred,
+            )
+            for job in self.jobs
+        )
+        self.jobs.clear()

+def install_movement_policies(manager, controller, *names, **limits):
+    now = [0.0]
+    controller.declarations._clock = lambda: now[0]
+    runtime = KVPolicyRuntime(
+        KVControlConfig(
+            policies=[
+                KVPolicyConfig(name=name, implementation="tool_wait") for name in names
+            ],
+            **limits,
+        ),
+        controller,
+        manager,
+        lambda: (),
+        clock=lambda: now[0],
+        wall_clock=lambda: 0,
+    )
+    controller.policies = runtime
+    return runtime, now

+def derived_results(controller, parent):
+    children = tuple(
+        controller.registry.get(ref.message_id, ref.action_id)
+        for ref in parent.derived_operations
+    )
+    for child, reference in zip(children, parent.derived_operations):
+        assert child.operation_id == reference.operation_id
+        assert child.origin.message_id == parent.message_id
+        assert child.origin.action_id == parent.action_id
+        assert child.origin.operation_id == parent.operation_id
+    return children

+def test_native_control_moves_real_gpu_buffers_before_publishing_hits(

+):
+    init_none_hash(sha256)

+    registry = OperationRegistry("buffer-engine", engine_epoch="buffer-epoch")
+    index = SessionPrefixIndex(uuid.uuid4().hex, "buffer-epoch")

+    config = SimpleNamespace(

+        ),
+    )
+    adapter = MooncakeControlAdapter(config, manager.kv_cache_config, 4)
+    executor = KVResourceController(manager, registry, declarations, (adapter,))
+    controller = NativeKVController(registry, index, declarations, executor=executor)
+    context = ControlContext("buffer-engine", "buffer-epoch", "native")
+    target = {
+        "kind": "hashes",
+        "namespace": index.namespace,
+        "blocks": [
+            {
+                "block_hash": request.block_hashes[0].hex(),
+                "group_id": 0,

+                "end_token": 4,
+            }
+        ],
+    }
+
+    def submit(action, extra):

+                "0.1",
+                action,
+                [
+                    KvHintAction("a", action, "1", {"target": target, **extra}),
+                ],
+            ),
+            context,
+        ).results[0]
+
+    workers, tensors, layouts, registered_keys = [], [], [], []
+    original_device = torch.accelerator.current_device_index()
+    try:
+        for rank, store in enumerate(stores):
+            torch.accelerator.set_device_index(rank)
+            tensor = torch.arange(64, device=f"cuda:{rank}", dtype=torch.float32)
+            tensor = tensor.reshape(4, 16).add(100 * rank).to(dtype)
+            assert store.register_buffer(tensor.data_ptr(), tensor.nbytes) == 0
+            tensors.append(tensor)
+            layout = RankLocalStoreLayout(
+                KeyMetadata("control-test", rank, 0, 0, 0), 4, 4
+            )
+            layout.register_kv_caches([tensor], 4)
+            layouts.append(layout)
+            workers.append(
+                MooncakeControlWorker(
+                    _DeviceCheckedStore(store, rank),
+                    {0: layout},
+                    rank=rank,
+                    tp_rank=rank,
+                    group_replication={0: 1},
+                )
+            )
+        blocks = manager.allocate_slots(request, 4)
+        assert blocks is not None
+        manager.cache_blocks(request, 4)
+        source_id = blocks.blocks[0][0].block_id
+        expected = [tensor[source_id].cpu().clone() for tensor in tensors]
+        manager.free(request)
+
+        def drain(action):
+            deadline = time.monotonic() + 20
+            while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+                for worker in workers:
+                    adapter.update(worker.poll())
+                executor.progress()
+                result = registry.get(action, "a")
+                if result.status.terminal and not adapter.has_pending:
+                    return result
+                time.sleep(0.01)
+            pytest.fail("Native control did not drain real Store transfers")
+
+        result = submit("demote", {"destination": "mooncake"})
+        assert result.status == OperationStatus.RUNNING
+        jobs = adapter.take_metadata()
+        assert len(jobs) == 1
+        for rank, worker in enumerate(workers):
+            torch.accelerator.set_device_index(rank)
+            worker.submit(jobs, "store")
+            key = layouts[rank].key_for(0, get_block_hash(keys[0]))
+            registered_keys.append(f"kv-control:{jobs[0].scope}@{key}")
+        result = drain("demote")
+        assert result.status == OperationStatus.COMPLETED
+        assert result.completed_steps == ("cold_copy_stored", "gpu_copies_reclaimed")
+        assert manager.get_computed_blocks(request)[1] == 0
+        for rank, tensor in enumerate(tensors):
+            torch.accelerator.set_device_index(rank)
+            tensor.zero_()
+        if outcome == "missing_rank":
+            stores[1].remove(registered_keys[1], True)
+        assert (
+            submit("prefetch", {"source": "mooncake"}).status == OperationStatus.RUNNING
+        )
+        jobs = adapter.take_metadata()
+        assert len(jobs) == 1
+        assert manager.get_computed_blocks(request)[1] == 0
+        for rank, worker in enumerate(workers):
+            torch.accelerator.set_device_index(rank)
+            worker.submit(jobs, "load")
+        if outcome == "reset":
+            assert not manager.reset_prefix_cache()
+        result = drain("prefetch")
+        expected_status = {
+            "success": OperationStatus.COMPLETED,
+            "missing_rank": OperationStatus.MISSING,
+            "reset": OperationStatus.CANCELLED,
+        }[outcome]
+        assert result.status == expected_status
+        assert manager.get_computed_blocks(request)[1] == (
+            4 if outcome == "success" else 0
+        )
+        assert not manager.get_transfer_manager().has_pending
+        if outcome == "success":
+            for rank, tensor in enumerate(tensors):
+                torch.testing.assert_close(
+                    tensor[jobs[0].block_id].cpu(),
+                    expected[rank],
+                    rtol=0,
+                    atol=0,
+                )
+    finally:
+        for worker in workers:
+            worker.close()
+        for store, tensor in zip(stores, tensors):
+            store.unregister_buffer(tensor.data_ptr())
+        for store, key in zip(stores, registered_keys):
+            store.remove(key, True)
+        torch.accelerator.set_device_index(original_device)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""Request-free connector work and rank-specific completion accounting."""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+
+from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_transfer import KVCacheTransferLease
+from vllm.v1.kv_hints.transfers import KVTransferCompletion
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class KVTransferRankResult:
+    transfer_id: int
+    generation: int
+    rank: int
+    success: bool
+    reason: str = ""
+    missing: bool = False
+    bytes_transferred: int = 0
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _PendingTransfer:
+    lease: KVCacheTransferLease
+    ranks: dict[int, KVTransferRankResult] = field(default_factory=dict)
+
+
+class KVTransferQueue:
+    def __init__(self, num_workers: int):
+        if num_workers < 1:
+            raise ValueError("Transfers require at least one worker")
+        self.num_workers = num_workers
+        self._queued: list[KVCacheTransferLease] = []
+        self._pending: dict[int, _PendingTransfer] = {}
+        self._completed: list[KVTransferCompletion] = []
+
+    @property
+    def has_pending(self) -> bool:
+        return bool(self._pending)
+
+    def submit(self, lease: KVCacheTransferLease) -> None:
+        if lease.transfer_id in self._pending:
+            raise ValueError("Physical transfer is already queued")
+        self._pending[lease.transfer_id] = _PendingTransfer(lease)
+        self._queued.append(lease)
+
+    def take_metadata(self) -> list[KVCacheTransferLease]:
+        queued, self._queued = self._queued, []
+        return queued
+
+    def update(self, results: list[KVTransferRankResult]) -> None:
+        for result in results:
+            pending = self._pending.get(result.transfer_id)
+            if (
+                pending is None
+                or pending.lease.generation != result.generation
+                or not 0 <= result.rank < self.num_workers
+            ):
+                continue
+            previous = pending.ranks.get(result.rank)
+            if previous is None or not result.success:
+                pending.ranks[result.rank] = result
+            if len(pending.ranks) != self.num_workers:
+                continue
+            failures = [r for r in pending.ranks.values() if not r.success]
+            self._completed.append(
+                KVTransferCompletion(
+                    result.transfer_id,
+                    result.generation,
+                    not failures,
+                    "; ".join(r.reason[:512] for r in failures[:3]),
+                    bool(failures) and all(r.missing for r in failures),
+                    sum(r.bytes_transferred for r in pending.ranks.values()),
+                )
+            )
+            del self._pending[result.transfer_id]
+
+    def poll(self) -> tuple[KVTransferCompletion, ...]:
+        completed, self._completed = tuple(self._completed), []
+        return completed

+"""Native control adapter using the Store connector's registered buffer layouts."""
+
+from concurrent.futures import Future, ThreadPoolExecutor
+from typing import Any, Literal
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.control import (
+    KVTransferQueue,
+    KVTransferRankResult,
+)
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake.store.data import StoreLayout
+from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_transfer import KVCacheTransferLease
+from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import (
+    BlockHashWithGroupId,
+    get_block_hash,
+    get_group_id,
+)
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import KVCacheConfig
+from vllm.v1.kv_hints.control import ControlError
+from vllm.v1.request import Request
+
+MOONCAKE_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND = -704
+
+
+class MooncakeControlAdapter(KVTransferQueue):
+    tier: Literal["cpu", "mooncake"] = "mooncake"
+    limitations: tuple[str, ...] = (
+        "Full group boundaries and primary cache entries only; PCP=DCP=1",
+        "Share establishes Store availability; destination GPU requires Prefetch",
+        "Control objects use a compatibility namespace separate from automatic offload",
+    )
+
+    def __init__(self, config: VllmConfig, cache: KVCacheConfig, hash_block_size: int):
+        super().__init__(config.parallel_config.world_size)
+        self.parallel = config.parallel_config
+        self.cache = cache
+        self.cache_hash_block_size = hash_block_size
+        assert config.kv_transfer_config is not None
+        transfer = config.kv_transfer_config
+        can_put = transfer.is_kv_producer or transfer.kv_connector_extra_config.get(
+            "save_decode_cache", False
+        )
+        self.actions: tuple[str, ...] = (
+            ("prefetch", "demote", "share") if can_put else ("prefetch",)
+        )
+
+    def validate(
+        self,
+        direction: Literal["load", "store"],
+        key: BlockHashWithGroupId,
+        num_tokens: int,
+    ) -> None:
+        group = get_group_id(key)
+        if (
+            self.parallel.prefill_context_parallel_size != 1
+            or self.parallel.decode_context_parallel_size != 1
+            or self.cache.hisparse_host_num_blocks is not None
+            or group not in self.cache.prefix_cacheable_group_ids
+            or num_tokens % self.cache.kv_cache_groups[group].kv_cache_spec.block_size
+        ):
+            raise ControlError(
+                "unsupported", "Unsupported Mooncake control boundary/layout"
+            )
+        if direction == "store" and "demote" not in self.actions:
+            raise ControlError("unsupported", "Connector is not configured to store KV")
+
+    def awaiting_load(self, request: Request) -> bool:
+        for pending in self._pending.values():
+            lease = pending.lease
+            if lease.direction != "load":
+                continue
+            hash_index = lease.num_tokens // self.cache_hash_block_size - 1
+            if 0 <= hash_index < len(request.block_hashes) and request.block_hashes[
+                hash_index
+            ] == get_block_hash(lease.key):
+                return True
+        return False
+
+
+class MooncakeControlWorker:
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        store: Any,
+        layouts: dict[int, StoreLayout],
+        *,
+        rank: int,
+        tp_rank: int,
+        group_replication: dict[int, int],
+        replicate_config: Any = None,
+        group_semantics: bool = False,
+    ):
+        self.store = store
+        self.layouts = layouts
+        self.rank = rank
+        self.tp_rank = tp_rank
+        self.group_replication = group_replication
+        self.replicate_config = replicate_config
+        self.group_semantics = group_semantics
+        self._executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(
+            max_workers=1, thread_name_prefix="kv-control"
+        )
+        self._pending: dict[int, Future[KVTransferRankResult]] = {}
+
+    def submit(self, leases: list[KVCacheTransferLease], direction: str) -> None:
+        selected = [lease for lease in leases if lease.direction == direction]
+        if not selected:
+            return
+        ready = torch.Event()
+        ready.record()
+        for lease in selected:
+            if lease.transfer_id not in self._pending:
+                self._pending[lease.transfer_id] = self._executor.submit(
+                    self._transfer, lease, ready
+                )
+
+    def _transfer(
+        self, lease: KVCacheTransferLease, ready: torch.Event
+    ) -> KVTransferRankResult:
+        try:
+            device = ready.device
+            if device is None or device.index is None:
+                raise ValueError("Control transfer requires a recorded device event")
+            torch.accelerator.set_device_index(device.index)
+            ready.synchronize()
+            group = get_group_id(lease.key)
+            layout = self.layouts[group]
+            if lease.num_tokens % layout.block_size:
+                raise ValueError("Control transfer splits a Store block")
+            factor = self.group_replication[group]
+            block_index = lease.num_tokens // layout.block_size - 1
+            if lease.direction == "store" and (
+                block_index % factor
+                != (self.tp_rank + layout.metadata.group_id) % factor
+            ):
+                return KVTransferRankResult(
+                    lease.transfer_id, lease.generation, self.rank, True
+                )
+            shards = layout.local_shard_ids
+            block_hash = get_block_hash(lease.key)
+            keys = [
+                f"kv-control:{lease.scope}@{layout.key_for(shard, block_hash)}"
+                for shard in shards
+            ]
+            addresses, sizes, _ = layout.prepare_values(
+                [(0, layout.block_size)] * len(shards), [lease.block_id], shards
+            )
+            if not addresses or any(not size for size in sizes):
+                raise ValueError("No registered Store buffers for this group")
+            if lease.direction == "load":
+                result = self.store.batch_get_into_multi_buffers(keys, addresses, sizes)
+            else:
+                if self.group_semantics:
+                    self.replicate_config.group_ids = [
+                        f"kv-control:{lease.scope}@{get_block_hash(lease.key).hex()}"
+                    ] * len(keys)
+                if self.replicate_config is None:
+                    result = self.store.batch_put_from_multi_buffers(
+                        keys, addresses, sizes
+                    )
+                else:
+                    result = self.store.batch_put_from_multi_buffers(
+                        keys, addresses, sizes, self.replicate_config
+                    )
+            failures = [value for value in result if value < 0]
+            if (
+                lease.direction == "load"
+                and len(result) == len(keys)
+                and failures
+                and all(value == MOONCAKE_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND for value in failures)
+            ):
+                return KVTransferRankResult(
+                    lease.transfer_id,
+                    lease.generation,
+                    self.rank,
+                    False,
+                    "Mooncake object is missing",
+                    missing=True,
+                )
+            if len(result) != len(keys) or failures:
+                raise RuntimeError(f"Mooncake {lease.direction} failed: {result}")
+            if lease.direction == "load" and any(
+                value != sum(size) for value, size in zip(result, sizes, strict=True)
+            ):
+                raise RuntimeError("Mooncake load returned an incomplete object")
+            return KVTransferRankResult(
+                lease.transfer_id,
+                lease.generation,
+                self.rank,
+                True,
+                bytes_transferred=sum(sum(size) for size in sizes),
+            )
+        except Exception as error:
+            return KVTransferRankResult(
+                lease.transfer_id,
+                lease.generation,
+                self.rank,
+                False,
+                f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"[:512],
+            )
+
+    def poll(self) -> list[KVTransferRankResult]:
+        completed = []
+        for transfer_id, future in tuple(self._pending.items()):
+            if future.done():
+                completed.append(future.result())
+                del self._pending[transfer_id]
+        return completed
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        self._executor.shutdown(wait=True)

+            raise ControlError("missing", "CPU content is missing")

+        indices = [0] * len(self._groups)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""HTTP ingress for the same explicit engine control used by Python clients."""
+
+from typing import Any, Literal
+
+import msgspec
+from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, FastAPI, Request
+from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
+
+from vllm.engine.protocol import EngineClient
+from vllm.entrypoints.serve.utils.api_utils import validate_json_request
+from vllm.v1.kv_hints.api import ControlInvocation
+from vllm.v1.kv_hints.control import ControlError
+
+router = APIRouter()
+
+
+class ControlRequest(msgspec.Struct, forbid_unknown_fields=True):  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+    method: Literal[
+        "submit",
+        "operation",
+        "associations",
+        "events",
+        "acknowledge",
+        "capacity",
+        "residency",
+        "cancel",
+    ]
+    invocation: ControlInvocation
+    payload: dict[str, Any]
+
+
+def error_response(code: str, message: str) -> JSONResponse:
+    status = {
+        "wrong_engine": 404,
+        "missing": 404,
+        "missing_association": 404,
+        "stale_epoch": 409,
+        "stale_revision": 409,
+        "stale_operation": 409,
+        "conflict": 409,
+        "event_gap": 409,
+        "unsupported": 501,
+        "unsupported_consumer": 501,
+        "capacity": 429,
+        "busy": 409,
+        "acknowledged": 409,
+        "payload_too_large": 413,
+    }.get(code, 400)
+    return JSONResponse(
+        {"error": {"code": code, "message": message}}, status_code=status
+    )
+
+
+@router.get("/v1/kv/capabilities")
+async def capabilities(raw_request: Request):
+    client: EngineClient | None = raw_request.app.state.engine_client
+    if client is None:
+        return {"engines": []}
+    try:
+        return {"engines": await client.get_kv_control_capabilities()}
+    except ControlError as error:
+        return error_response(error.code, str(error))
+
+
+@router.post("/v1/kv/control", dependencies=[Depends(validate_json_request)])
+async def control(raw_request: Request):
+    settings = raw_request.app.state.vllm_config.kv_control_config
+    if settings is None:
+        return error_response("unsupported", "Programmable KV control is disabled")
+    data = bytearray()
+    async for chunk in raw_request.stream():
+        if len(data) + len(chunk) > settings.max_envelope_bytes + 2048:
+            return error_response(
+                "payload_too_large", "Control request byte limit exceeded"
+            )
+        data.extend(chunk)
+    try:
+        request = msgspec.json.decode(data, type=ControlRequest)
+    except msgspec.DecodeError as error:
+        return error_response("invalid_payload", str(error)[:4096])
+    client: EngineClient = raw_request.app.state.engine_client
+    try:
+        result = await client.kv_control(
+            request.method, msgspec.to_builtins(request.invocation), request.payload
+        )
+        return JSONResponse(result)
+    except ControlError as error:
+        return error_response(error.code, str(error))
+
+
+def attach_router(app: FastAPI):
+    app.include_router(router)

+"""Revisioned copy-lifetime claims feeding the existing retention queue.
+
+Claim/TTL semantics follow vllm-project/vllm#59714 (7966f717dd4e). Eviction
+continues through RetentionFreeBlockQueue, shared with logical declarations.
+"""
+
+import heapq
+import time
+from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import KVCacheBlock
+from vllm.v1.kv_hints.actions import SetPriority
+from vllm.v1.kv_hints.control import ControlError
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class _Claim:
+    revision: int
+    value: int | None
+    ttl: float | None
+    expires_at: float
+    policy_name: str | None
+    owners: tuple[str, ...]
+
+
+class KVCachePriority:
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic,
+        max_claims_per_copy: int = 16,
+    ):
+        self.clock = clock
+        self.max_claims_per_copy = max_claims_per_copy
+        self._claims: dict[int, dict[str, _Claim]] = {}
+        self._expiry: list[tuple[float, int, int, str]] = []
+        self._priorities: dict[int, int] = {}
+        self._changed: set[int] = set()
+        self._sequence = 0
+
+    def apply(
+        self,
+        action: SetPriority,
+        blocks: Iterable[KVCacheBlock],
+        *,
+        policy_name: str | None = None,
+        owners: tuple[str, ...] = (),
+    ) -> tuple[int, ...]:
+        self.expire()
+        now = self.clock()
+        selected = {
+            b.block_id for b in blocks if not b.is_null and b.block_hash is not None
+        }
+        if not selected:
+            raise ControlError("missing", "No cached local G1 copies")
+        changed = []
+        for block_id in selected:
+            claims = self._claims.get(block_id, {})
+            old = claims.get(action.claim_id)
+            if old is not None:
+                if policy_name is not None and old.policy_name != policy_name:
+                    raise ControlError(
+                        "busy", "A policy cannot replace another caller's claim"
+                    )
+                if action.revision < old.revision:
+                    continue
+                if action.revision == old.revision:
+                    if (action.value, action.ttl_seconds) != (old.value, old.ttl):
+                        raise ControlError(
+                            "conflict", "Conflicting payload for claim revision"
+                        )
+                    continue
+            elif len(claims) >= self.max_claims_per_copy:
+                raise ControlError("capacity", "Per-copy claim limit reached")
+            changed.append(block_id)
+        claim = _Claim(
+            action.revision,
+            action.value,
+            action.ttl_seconds,
+            now + (action.ttl_seconds or 0),
+            policy_name,
+            owners,
+        )
+        for block_id in changed:
+            self._claims.setdefault(block_id, {})[action.claim_id] = claim
+            if action.value is not None:
+                self._sequence += 1
+                heapq.heappush(
+                    self._expiry,
+                    (claim.expires_at, self._sequence, block_id, action.claim_id),
+                )
+            self._refresh(block_id, now)
+        self._compact()
+        return tuple(sorted(changed))
+
+    def priority(self, block: KVCacheBlock) -> int | None:
+        return self._priorities.get(block.block_id)
+
+    def has_explicit(self, blocks: Iterable[KVCacheBlock]) -> bool:
+        now = self.clock()
+        return any(
+            c.policy_name is None and c.value is not None and c.expires_at > now
+            for block in blocks
+            for c in self._claims.get(block.block_id, {}).values()
+        )
+
+    def _refresh(self, block_id: int, now: float) -> None:
+        values = [
+            c.value
+            for c in self._claims.get(block_id, {}).values()
+            if c.value is not None and c.expires_at > now
+        ]
+        old = self._priorities.get(block_id)
+        if values:
+            self._priorities[block_id] = max(values)
+        else:
+            self._priorities.pop(block_id, None)
+        if old != self._priorities.get(block_id):
+            self._changed.add(block_id)
+
+    def expire(self) -> None:
+        now = self.clock()
+        while self._expiry and self._expiry[0][0] <= now:
+            _, _, block_id, _ = heapq.heappop(self._expiry)
+            self._refresh(block_id, now)
+        self._compact()
+
+    def take_changes(self) -> set[int]:
+        self.expire()
+        changed, self._changed = self._changed, set()
+        return changed
+
+    def forget(self, block: KVCacheBlock) -> None:
+        self._claims.pop(block.block_id, None)
+        self._priorities.pop(block.block_id, None)
+        self._changed.discard(block.block_id)
+        self._compact()
+
+    def finish_owners(self, owners: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
+        for block_id, claims in self._claims.items():
+            for identity, claim in tuple(claims.items()):
+                if claim.policy_name is not None and set(claim.owners).intersection(
+                    owners
+                ):
+                    # Retain the revision tombstone until this copy is forgotten.
+                    claims[identity] = _Claim(
+                        claim.revision, None, None, 0, claim.policy_name, claim.owners
+                    )
+            self._refresh(block_id, self.clock())
+
+    def _compact(self) -> None:
+        bound = max(64, 2 * len(self._claims) * self.max_claims_per_copy)
+        if len(self._expiry) > bound:
+            self._expiry = []
+            for block_id, claims in self._claims.items():
+                for identity, claim in claims.items():
+                    if claim.value is not None:
+                        self._sequence += 1
+                        self._expiry.append(
+                            (claim.expires_at, self._sequence, block_id, identity)
+                        )
+            heapq.heapify(self._expiry)

+"""Engine-owned eviction ordering for optional retention declarations."""
+
+import heapq
+from collections.abc import Callable
+
+from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import FreeKVCacheBlockQueue, KVCacheBlock
+
+
+class RetentionFreeBlockQueue(FreeKVCacheBlockQueue):
+    """Keep ordinary queue order as the tie-breaker for eviction priorities.
+
+    The linked list remains authoritative for free membership. Lazy heap entries
+    are bounded by compaction; retention never changes a block's reference count.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        free_blocks: list[KVCacheBlock],
+        all_blocks: list[KVCacheBlock],
+        priority: Callable[[KVCacheBlock], int],
+        synchronize: Callable[[], None],
+    ):
+        super().__init__(free_blocks)
+        self._all_blocks = all_blocks
+        self._priority = priority
+        self._synchronize = synchronize
+        self._keys: dict[int, tuple[int, int]] = {
+            block.block_id: (priority(block), order)
+            for order, block in enumerate(free_blocks)
+        }
+        self._head_order = 0
+        self._tail_order = len(free_blocks)
+        self._heap = [
+            (p, order, block_id) for block_id, (p, order) in self._keys.items()
+        ]
+        heapq.heapify(self._heap)
+        self.last_displaced_cached_blocks = 0
+
+    def priority(self, block: KVCacheBlock) -> int:
+        self._synchronize()
+        return self._priority(block)
+
+    def popleft(self) -> KVCacheBlock:
+        return self.popleft_n(1)[0]
+
+    def popleft_n(self, n: int) -> list[KVCacheBlock]:
+        if n < 0 or n > self.num_free_blocks:
+            raise ValueError("Not enough free blocks")
+        self.last_displaced_cached_blocks = 0
+        if n == 0:
+            return []
+        self._synchronize()
+        selected: list[KVCacheBlock] = []
+        while len(selected) < n:
+            priority, order, block_id = heapq.heappop(self._heap)
+            if self._keys.get(block_id) != (priority, order):
+                continue
+            block = self._all_blocks[block_id]
+            super().remove(block)
+            del self._keys[block_id]
+            self.last_displaced_cached_blocks += block.block_hash is not None
+            selected.append(block)
+        self._compact()
+        return selected
+
+    def remove(self, block: KVCacheBlock) -> None:
+        super().remove(block)
+        del self._keys[block.block_id]
+        self._compact()
+
+    def append(self, block: KVCacheBlock) -> None:
+        super().append(block)
+        self._add([block], prepend=False)
+
+    def append_n(self, blocks: list[KVCacheBlock]) -> None:
+        super().append_n(blocks)
+        self._add(blocks, prepend=False)
+
+    def prepend_n(self, blocks: list[KVCacheBlock]) -> None:
+        super().prepend_n(blocks)
+        self._add(blocks, prepend=True)
+
+    def cache_changed(self, block: KVCacheBlock) -> None:
+        previous = self._keys.get(block.block_id)
+        if previous is None:
+            return
+        priority = self._priority(block)
+        if previous[0] != priority:
+            self._keys[block.block_id] = (priority, previous[1])
+            heapq.heappush(self._heap, (priority, previous[1], block.block_id))
+            self._compact()
+
+    def rebuild(self) -> None:
+        self._keys = {
+            block_id: (self._priority(self._all_blocks[block_id]), order)
+            for block_id, (_, order) in self._keys.items()
+        }
+        self._heap = [
+            (p, order, block_id) for block_id, (p, order) in self._keys.items()
+        ]
+        heapq.heapify(self._heap)
+
+    def _add(self, blocks: list[KVCacheBlock], *, prepend: bool) -> None:
+        if prepend:
+            self._head_order -= len(blocks)
+            first = self._head_order
+        else:
+            first = self._tail_order
+            self._tail_order += len(blocks)
+        for offset, block in enumerate(blocks):
+            order, priority = first + offset, self._priority(block)
+            self._keys[block.block_id] = (priority, order)
+            heapq.heappush(self._heap, (priority, order, block.block_id))
+        self._compact()
+
+    def _compact(self) -> None:
+        if len(self._heap) > max(64, 2 * len(self._keys)):
+            self._heap = [
+                (p, order, block_id) for block_id, (p, order) in self._keys.items()
+            ]
+            heapq.heapify(self._heap)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Request-independent transfer references owned by the KV cache manager."""
+
+from collections.abc import Iterable
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Literal
+
+from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import (
+    BlockHashWithGroupId,
+    KVCacheBlock,
+    get_group_id,
+)
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_manager import KVCacheManager
+
+
+class KVCacheTransferError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str):
+        super().__init__(message)
+        self.code = code
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class KVCacheTransferLease:
+    transfer_id: int
+    generation: int
+    direction: Literal["load", "store"]
+    scope: str
+    key: BlockHashWithGroupId
+    num_tokens: int
+    block_id: int
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _Transfer:
+    lease: KVCacheTransferLease
+    block: KVCacheBlock
+    interests: set[int] = field(default_factory=set)
+    started: bool = False
+    completed: bool = False
+
+
+class KVCacheTransferManager:
+    """Hold buffers until all worker access ends, independently of callers.
+
+    Callers join one physical transfer per direction/content key. The executor
+    must call ``complete`` only after every participating worker has stopped
+    accessing the buffer, including workers whose transfer failed or was cancelled.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, manager: "KVCacheManager"):
+        self.manager = manager
+        self.pool = manager.block_pool
+        self.generation = 0
+        self._next_id = 0
+        self._transfers: dict[int, _Transfer] = {}
+        self._by_key: dict[tuple[str, str, BlockHashWithGroupId], int] = {}
+        self._loads: dict[BlockHashWithGroupId, int] = {}
+        self.max_load_blocks = 0
+
+    @property
+    def has_pending(self) -> bool:
+        return bool(self._transfers)
+
+    def held_block_counts(self) -> tuple[int, int]:
+        """Return destination and source counts, already charged in pool usage."""
+        loads = {
+            t.block.block_id
+            for t in self._transfers.values()
+            if t.lease.direction == "load"
+        }
+        stores = {
+            t.block.block_id
+            for t in self._transfers.values()
+            if t.lease.direction == "store"
+        }
+        return len(loads), len(stores)
+
+    @property
+    def reserved_load_blocks(self) -> int:
+        return len(self._loads)
+
+    def load_requirements(
+        self,
+        blocks: Iterable[tuple[BlockHashWithGroupId, int]],
+        *,
+        scope: str,
+    ) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
+        """Return new load slots and free blocks a complete preparation needs."""
+        loads = committed = 0
+        for key, num_tokens in blocks:
+            existing = self._by_key.get(("load", scope, key))
+            if existing is not None:
+                transfer = self._transfers[existing]
+                if (
+                    transfer.lease.generation != self.generation
+                    or not transfer.interests
+                ):
+                    return None
+                continue
+            copies = self.pool.cached_block_hash_to_block.get_blocks(key)
+            source = next(
+                (
+                    b
+                    for b in copies
+                    if b.block_hash == key and b.block_hash_num_tokens == num_tokens
+                ),
+                None,
+            )
+            if source is not None:
+                committed += source.ref_cnt == 0
+            elif key in self._loads:
+                return None
+            elif not copies:
+                loads += 1
+                committed += 1
+        return loads, committed
+
+    def is_loading(self, key: BlockHashWithGroupId) -> bool:
+        identifier = self._loads.get(key)
+        transfer = self._transfers.get(identifier) if identifier is not None else None
+        return bool(
+            transfer is not None
+            and transfer.lease.generation == self.generation
+            and transfer.interests
+            and not transfer.completed
+        )
+
+    def acquire(
+        self,
+        direction: Literal["load", "store"],
+        key: BlockHashWithGroupId,
+        num_tokens: int,
+        interest: int,
+        *,
+        scope: str,
+    ) -> tuple[KVCacheTransferLease | None, bool]:
+        """Approve one buffer, returning its lease and whether work is new.
+
+        A load of already resident content returns ``(None, False)``. Capacity,
+        missing sources, invalid coordinates and draining work raise an error
+        without acquiring resources. Repeated interests do not add references.
+        """
+        group = get_group_id(key)
+        if direction not in ("load", "store"):
+            raise KVCacheTransferError("unsupported", "Unknown transfer direction")
+        if (
+            not self.manager.enable_caching
+            or not 0 <= group < self.manager.num_kv_cache_groups
+            or not self.manager.kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups[
+                group
+            ].kv_cache_spec.prefix_cacheable
+            or self.manager.coordinator.single_type_managers[group].block_pool
+            is not self.pool
+        ):
+            raise KVCacheTransferError("unsupported", "Group is not prefix cacheable")
+        if not 0 < num_tokens <= self.manager.max_model_len or (
+            num_tokens % self.pool.hash_block_size
+        ):
+            raise KVCacheTransferError("invalid_payload", "Invalid content boundary")
+
+        lookup = (direction, scope, key)
+        existing = self._by_key.get(lookup)
+        if existing is not None:
+            transfer = self._transfers[existing]
+            if transfer.lease.num_tokens != num_tokens:
+                raise KVCacheTransferError("invalid_payload", "Conflicting coordinates")
+            if transfer.lease.generation != self.generation or not transfer.interests:
+                raise KVCacheTransferError("busy", "Previous transfer is draining")
+            if transfer.completed:
+                return None, False
+            transfer.interests.add(interest)
+            return transfer.lease, False
+
+        copies = self.pool.cached_block_hash_to_block.get_blocks(key)
+        # A primary entry has an exact boundary. Aliases lack separate boundary
+        # metadata, so adapters must request the primary entry for movement.
+        source = next(
+            (
+                block
+                for block in copies
+                if block.block_hash == key and block.block_hash_num_tokens == num_tokens
+            ),
+            None,
+        )
+        if copies and source is None:
+            raise KVCacheTransferError(
+                "unsupported", "Transfer requires an exact primary cache boundary"
+            )
+        if direction == "load":
+            if source is not None:
+                return None, False
+            if key in self._loads:
+                raise KVCacheTransferError("busy", "Another source is loading this key")
+            if self.max_load_blocks and len(self._loads) >= self.max_load_blocks:
+                raise KVCacheTransferError(
+                    "capacity", "In-flight load budget exhausted"
+                )
+            if self.pool.get_num_free_blocks() <= self.manager.watermark_blocks:
+                raise KVCacheTransferError("capacity", "No destination capacity")
+            block = self.pool.get_new_blocks(1)[0]
+        else:
+            if source is None:
+                raise KVCacheTransferError("missing", "Source is not resident")
+            block = source
+            self.pool.touch([block])
+
+        self._next_id += 1
+        lease = KVCacheTransferLease(
+            self._next_id,
+            self.generation,
+            direction,
+            scope,
+            key,
+            num_tokens,
+            block.block_id,
+        )
+        self._transfers[lease.transfer_id] = _Transfer(lease, block, {interest})
+        self._by_key[lookup] = lease.transfer_id
+        if direction == "load":
+            self._loads[key] = lease.transfer_id
+        return lease, True
+
+    def hold_resident(
+        self, key: BlockHashWithGroupId, num_tokens: int, interest: int, *, scope: str
+    ) -> KVCacheTransferLease:
+        """Keep an already validated resident member of a preparation stable."""
+        lookup = ("load", scope, key)
+        existing = self._by_key.get(lookup)
+        if existing is not None:
+            transfer = self._transfers[existing]
+            if (
+                not transfer.completed
+                or transfer.lease.generation != self.generation
+                or transfer.lease.num_tokens != num_tokens
+            ):
+                raise KVCacheTransferError("busy", "Resident copy is not ready")
+            transfer.interests.add(interest)
+            return transfer.lease
+        source = next(
+            (
+                block
+                for block in self.pool.cached_block_hash_to_block.get_blocks(key)
+                if block.block_hash == key and block.block_hash_num_tokens == num_tokens
+            ),
+            None,
+        )
+        if source is None:
+            raise KVCacheTransferError(
+                "missing", "Resident copy is no longer available"
+            )
+        self.pool.touch([source])
+        self._next_id += 1
+        lease = KVCacheTransferLease(
+            self._next_id,
+            self.generation,
+            "load",
+            scope,
+            key,
+            num_tokens,
+            source.block_id,
+        )
+        self._transfers[lease.transfer_id] = _Transfer(
+            lease, source, {interest}, started=True, completed=True
+        )
+        self._by_key[lookup] = lease.transfer_id
+        return lease
+
+    def start(self, lease: KVCacheTransferLease) -> bool:
+        """Mark dispatch before a worker can access the buffer, exactly once."""
+        transfer = self._get(lease)
+        if transfer is None or transfer.started or not transfer.interests:
+            return False
+        if lease.generation != self.generation:
+            return False
+        transfer.started = True
+        return True
+
+    def cancel(self, lease: KVCacheTransferLease, interest: int) -> None:
+        transfer = self._get(lease)
+        if transfer is None:
+            return
+        transfer.interests.discard(interest)
+        if not transfer.interests:
+            if transfer.completed:
+                self._release(transfer)
+            elif not transfer.started:
+                self.complete(lease, success=False)
+
+    def invalidate(self) -> None:
+        """Reject stale publication while retaining every dispatched buffer."""
+        self.generation += 1
+        for transfer in tuple(self._transfers.values()):
+            transfer.interests.clear()
+            if transfer.completed:
+                self._release(transfer)
+            elif not transfer.started:
+                self.complete(transfer.lease, success=False)
+
+    def complete(
+        self, lease: KVCacheTransferLease, *, success: bool, retain: bool = False
+    ) -> bool:
+        """Drain a physical transfer; return whether its outcome is still valid."""
+        transfer = self._get(lease)
+        if transfer is None or transfer.completed:
+            return False
+        valid = (
+            success
+            and transfer.started
+            and bool(transfer.interests)

+# Native KV hint primitives
+
+This experimental implementation of [RFC #57103](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57103) adds RFC #59708 primitives to the existing `KvHintsEnvelope` (`protocol_version: "0.1"`).
+Native action version **1.0** provides `vllm.set_priority`, `vllm.copy_to` and `vllm.move_to`.
+It follows #59714's priority payload and successful-completion semantics, and extends execution to existing CPU/Mooncake adapters and correlated asynchronous results.
+The COPY/MOVE payloads below define this branch's experimental interface; the upstream schema remains under discussion.
+
+Enable `--kv-control-config '{"engine_id":"worker-a"}'` (Python accepts the same configuration).
+Without it, existing hint forwarding is unchanged.
+Local policies are optional and disabled by default.
+No changes to Mooncake itself are required.
+
+See [benchmark and validation commands](../../../benchmarks/programmable_kv_cache/README.md) for serving examples and regression checks.
+
+## Terms
+
+- A native action is interpreted by vLLM; a backend action is forwarded for the selected backend to interpret.
+- G1 is the engine's local GPU cache; a cold tier stores copies in CPU memory or Mooncake Store.
+- A transfer hold keeps a buffer allocated while a worker may access it.
+- Publication registers successfully loaded data as reusable GPU cache.
+- A claim is one caller's priority declaration for a physical copy; its revision orders updates and rejects stale retries.
+- An operation incarnation is one submission instance identified by its operation ID.
+
+## Ownership and entry points
+
+`NativeKVController` checks control-record capacity and manages operation context and results.
+`KvHintDispatcher` registers primitive payload schemas and selects when each action executes.
+EngineCore consumes native request hints once and passes the same dispatcher to Scheduler for completion callbacks.
+Scheduler uses that dispatcher without parsing the envelope again.
+The configuration selects the envelope's interpreter: the `attached_consumer` startup default for request hints, or `consumer` in independent control invocation.
+The existing connector hook forwards backend envelopes without interpreting their action payloads, even when an action name resembles a native action.
+Mixed native/backend ownership is not supported.
+
+Request-attached GPU-source COPY/MOVE and SET_PRIORITY validate at ingress and queue until successful stop or length-limit completion.
+They execute before the scheduler releases request references.
+Abort/error cancel them; preemption keeps them pending.
+Cold-source COPY executes at ingress; a compatible resume waits for that load and falls back to ordinary computation if preparation fails.
+
+COPY executes at request entry or successful completion according to its transfer direction.
+Control-record limits bound pending work; resetting the cache generation invalidates it.
+A transfer started at request completion retains its source buffers after the request ends.
+The connector keeps the engine loop running until that work finishes.
+
+Independent Python/HTTP submission is an extension using the same dispatcher, resource approval and adapters; it executes immediately.
+`request_cached` requires an attached request.
+Logical selectors can be used independently.
+
+## Targets and locations
+
+Targets are `"request_cached"`, or the existing tagged request/hash/session selectors:
+
+- `request_cached` selects the actual cached copies still in the bound request's block tables.
+  Detached Mamba checkpoints are not in that scope.
+- `{"kind":"request","request_id":"$request","end_token":784}` selects logical token content in the bound request.
+  At completion it also resolves cached checkpoints that have left the active tables.
+  Explicit ranges are half-open.
+- A `hashes` target carries compatibility namespace and hash/group/token spans; a `session` target selects tracked continuation/range state.
+  Those targets are snapshotted at submission even when execution waits for request completion.
+
+Applications must discover group sizes and supported boundaries; `784` is the recorded local Qwen profile, not a universal block size.
+Physical block IDs are not public selectors.
+Unknown/unrepresented/unaligned ranges are reported.
+
+COPY/MOVE locations contain `tier` (`gpu`, `cpu`, `mooncake`) and optional `engine_id`.
+Omission means the addressed engine/configured backend.
+A different engine ID is rejected; destination GPU resources must be approved by that engine.
+Capabilities list the supported `directions`, targets and adapter limitations.
+
+## R1 MOVE / R2 COPY example
+
+Attach to R1, to save and reclaim its prefix after successful generation:
+
+```json
+{
+  "protocol_version": "0.1",
+  "message_id": "round-1-save",
+  "actions": [
+    {
+      "action_id": "move-prefix",
+      "action_type": "vllm.move_to",
+      "action_version": "1.0",
+      "payload": {
+        "target": {
+          "kind": "request",
+          "request_id": "$request",
+          "end_token": 784
+        },
+        "src": {
+          "tier": "gpu"
+        },
+        "dst": {
+          "tier": "mooncake"
+        }
+      }
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+R2 uses `vllm.copy_to`, the same logical range, `src={"tier":"mooncake"}` and `dst={"tier":"gpu"}`.
+It waits for the compatible load and uses GPU KV after the data is registered as reusable.
+This example starts COPY when R2 arrives, so it verifies execution and reuse without measuring savings from prefetch before request arrival.
+
+GPU-to-cold COPY preserves the source.
+MOVE saves first and reclaims only eligible copies.
+Cold-to-GPU MOVE is unsupported because selective cold deletion is absent.
+Cross-engine reuse is two COPYs (A→Store, then Store→B); Store availability never means B's GPU is ready.
+General CPU uses the existing CPU offload path; SimpleCPU and KVCR do not acquire new native movement capabilities through this branch.
+
+## SET_PRIORITY
+
+The #59714-compatible payload is:
+
+```json
+{
+  "target": "request_cached",
+  "location": "local_g1",
+  "claim_id": "router/task-1",
+  "revision": 1,
+  "value": 10,
+  "ttl_seconds": 60
+}
+```
+
+A signed integer value sets the eviction priority of a physical cache copy.
+A finite positive TTL starts when the priority takes effect.
+Copies with higher effective priority are evicted later; normal free-list/LRU ordering breaks ties.
+`value: null`, no TTL and a higher revision clear only this claim.
+Equal/older revisions do not renew TTL; conflicting payloads at an equal revision reject the operation before changing any selected claim.
+An explicit claim ends when a higher revision clears it with null, its TTL expires, or its physical copy is invalidated.
+An arbitrary claim ID does not associate the claim with a logical task, so task completion cannot infer that ownership.
+Task cleanup also removes the associated local-policy claims.
+The controller retains the latest revision for each claim ID, including cleared claims, until the copy is invalidated, reused or reset.
+This retained revision prevents stale updates from recreating a cleared claim; each copy supports at most 16 claim IDs.
+Reconstructed copies do not inherit these claims.
+
+Logical selectors are an extension selecting currently resident copies.
+Legacy Retain/Release declarations retain their independent logical-content lifetimes and can follow newly appended content when configured.
+Both declaration families feed **one** `RetentionFreeBlockQueue`, using the maximum valid priority; the default 0 applies only when no declaration exists.
+Priority never pins memory, allocates blocks, or changes active references.
+
+## Outcomes, retries and limits
+
+Queries/events use the common OperationRegistry, including message/action IDs, action type/version, engine epoch, namespace and optional originating policy.
+
+| Status | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| received | Admitted and correlated |
+| queued | Waiting for request completion, session admission, or a compatible COPY prerequisite; nonterminal, no reservation |
+| accepted / running | Approved work; not yet a guarantee of complete reusable scope |
+| completed / partial | Terminal outcome with actual stages and target scope |
+| deferred | Terminal resource refusal; retry intentionally with a new message ID |
+| missing / unsupported / failed / cancelled | Distinct terminal negative outcomes |
+
+`target_outcomes` identifies hash/group/token range, status, completed stages, reason and transfer ID/generation where physical work was dispatched.
+Already resident content is labeled and has no transfer ID.
+Missing ranges have no hash.
+MOVE can report a stored copy and still-referenced source as partial; COPY only reports GPU availability after all participating ranks stop accessing buffers and successful data is registered.
+Cancellation drains worker holds before reuse.
+Historical completion does not guarantee continued residency.
+
+`max_result_targets` (default 16384) rejects excessive movement scope before any allocation.
+Existing envelope/action/result/index limits still apply.
+Identical message/context replay returns existing results and never requeues or renews TTL.
+
+Call `acknowledge` with a message ID after collecting terminal results for every action in that message.
+This releases detailed records while keeping a bounded replay fingerprint until the original expiry.
+Identical replay then returns `acknowledged`; it does not execute again.
+`cancel` requires message ID, action ID and operation ID, so a delayed caller cannot cancel a newer operation instance.
+Cancelling a signal does not cancel its separately identified derived operations or roll back completed effects.
+
+`residency` resolves a bounded logical target into current GPU copies, references, effective priorities and native load progress.
+The query reports current state without reserving the copies.
+Cold-tier residency queries and physical residency events are not supported.
+`capacity` reports record/replay occupancy and actual unique physical transfer payload bytes.
+Per-operation bytes can attribute a shared transfer to more than one caller.
+
+Weight updates require idle requests and drained transfers.
+Use the existing start/update/finish lifecycle; the controller invalidates local KV, encoder and multimodal caches before transfer and rejects new inference/control submissions until a new version commits.
+Commit creates a fresh epoch and namespace and isolates ordinary connector hashes without deleting another engine's Store objects.
+The default version preserves legacy hashes.
+A previous version may be reused only with exactly its original weights.
+Tensor changes that bypass the start/update/finish lifecycle do not receive these protections.
+After a failed update, the engine rejects new work until the update completes or the engine restarts.
+
+Legacy action version `1` remains supported (`retain`, `release`, `evict`, `demote`, `prefetch`, `share`, state commands and signals).
+Explicit eviction has no implicit mapping to clearing priority.
+Optional retention/tool-wait policies now produce version-1.0 primitives through the same execution boundary.
+A SET_PRIORITY proposal waits for overlapping GPU COPY proposals from the same signal before application; its TTL starts after the copy is ready, and failed copies yield explicit missing or partial priority outcomes.
+Waiting proposals do not consume the execution budget, so a one-action-per-step limit cannot starve their prerequisites.
+There is no automatic tool-call detector.
+Request-free control and local policy production are explicit extensions to the initial request-attached RFC profile.
+
+Policies may declare `consumed_signals` as an immutable set of signal names.
+Signals with no configured consumer return `unconsumed` without building a request observation or invalidating scheduler guidance.
+The default `None` preserves delivery of every signal to existing third-party policies.
+Subclasses must explicitly redeclare the filter to opt in, so an overridden handler does not silently inherit a narrower signal set.
+
+The built-in tool-wait policy accepts `resume_after_seconds` on the initial
+`tool_wait` signal. It skips a speculative round trip when that estimate does
+not exceed `min_pause_seconds` (default 0.5) or its observed store-plus-load time.
+`consider_pause_duration=false` selects the pressure-only ablation. Missing
+estimates keep pressure-based demotion. Skipped movement history is bounded and
+cleaned with its logical owners; explicit movement commands are unaffected.
+This heuristic does not estimate GPU recomputation cost or guarantee residency.
+In admission-coupled mode a short tool can also use a sustained GPU backlog:
+current referenced occupancy must reach `min_pressure`, and an observed waiting
+request must have waited longer than the minimum window or measured store/load
+round trip, whichever is larger. With low current occupancy a short pause keeps
+G1 content even when projected demand is high. Observed queue age is a heuristic
+for this decision, not a prediction of the target request's remaining wait.
+
+`prefetch_on_admission=true` enables scheduler coordination for the movement
+policy. Under queued demand, a matching session's GPU COPY waits until that
+session is selected for admission. The scheduler starts preparation before cache
+lookup and waits for terminal publication; failure permits ordinary recomputation.
+Without queued demand the predicted preparation may execute early. Cancellation
+and task cleanup release queued scope without acquiring transfer buffers.
+Custom policies emitting `PolicyProposal.wait_for_admission` must enable
+`uses_scheduler_guidance` at startup. Only GPU COPY proposals support this flag.
+
+A concrete policy may implement `needs_request_observation(payload)` and return
+false when it does not read request or session demand. The observation still
+contains time and physical counters, but request/session tuples are empty and
+arrival history is preserved. Alternatively, it can implement
+`needs_request_observation_for_view(payload, counters)` to refine that decision
+using a counters-only observation before request queries. Subclasses default to
+full observations unless they explicitly implement one of these methods.
+A concrete scheduler policy may also set
+`signal_updates_guidance=false` if its signals cannot change request guidance.
+The built-in quota importance signal continues to invalidate cached guidance.
+
+Source references: [RFC #59708](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59708), [PR #59714 at 7966f717dd4e](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/7966f717dd4eb09461dd97102db1352c924bbf50/vllm/v1/kv_hints).
+Copy claims use the existing eviction queue; the branch does not add the draft PR's separate victim-selection heap.

+"""RFC #59708 primitive contracts; no allocator or connector dependencies."""
+
+import math
+from typing import Literal, TypeAlias
+
+import msgspec
+
+from vllm.v1.kv_hints.native import Identifier, Target, Tier, TokenPosition
+
+PRIMITIVE_VERSION = "1.0"
+PrimitiveTarget: TypeAlias = Target | Literal["request_cached"]
+
+
+class CacheLocation(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True, forbid_unknown_fields=True):  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+    tier: Tier
+    engine_id: Identifier | None = None
+
+
+class SetPriority(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True, forbid_unknown_fields=True):  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+    """Copy-scoped claim contract aligned with PR #59714's SetPriority."""
+
+    target: PrimitiveTarget
+    location: Literal["local_g1"]
+    claim_id: Identifier
+    revision: TokenPosition
+    value: int | None
+    ttl_seconds: float | None = None
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        if self.value is None:
+            if self.ttl_seconds is not None:
+                raise ValueError("Clearing a claim must omit ttl_seconds")
+        elif (
+            self.ttl_seconds is None
+            or not math.isfinite(self.ttl_seconds)
+            or self.ttl_seconds <= 0
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Setting a priority requires a finite positive TTL")
+
+
+class CopyTo(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True, forbid_unknown_fields=True):  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+    target: PrimitiveTarget
+    src: CacheLocation
+    dst: CacheLocation
+
+
+class MoveTo(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True, forbid_unknown_fields=True):  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+    target: PrimitiveTarget
+    src: CacheLocation
+    dst: CacheLocation
+
+
+Primitive: TypeAlias = SetPriority | CopyTo | MoveTo
+PRIMITIVES: dict[str, type[Primitive]] = {
+    "vllm.set_priority": SetPriority,
+    "vllm.copy_to": CopyTo,
+    "vllm.move_to": MoveTo,
+}
